nodes.summary: Starts the minute-interval unref'd RSS watchdog that writes a V8 heap snapshot into the log directory when memory exceeds the 2 GiB limit, taking at most one snapshot per threshold crossing.

nodes.name: resolveNetworkOptionsNoConfig
nodes.summary: Merges CLI flags over config-file server settings, detecting explicitly passed argv flags to decide precedence, defaulting the hostname to 0.0.0.0 when mDNS is enabled, and concatenating CORS allowlists.

nodes.name: logo
nodes.summary: Renders the opencode ASCII logo from block glyphs using per-half ANSI foreground/background colors with distinct shadow tones, falling back to a plain wordmark when stdout and stderr are not TTYs.

nodes.name: input
nodes.summary: Prompts the user for a line of input through a readline interface and resolves the trimmed answer as a promise.

nodes.name: upgrade
nodes.summary: Runs the auto-update check: skips when disabled by config or flag, publishes UpdateAvailable for notify-only or non-patch releases, otherwise performs the installation upgrade and publishes the Updated event.

nodes.name: hints
nodes.summary: Extracts argument placeholder hints ($1, $2, ... deduplicated and sorted, plus $ARGUMENTS) from a command template string.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Post-parse agent normalization: moves unknown keys into options so they survive round-trips, converts the deprecated tools boolean map into permission allow/deny rules (write/edit/patch collapse into permission.edit), and coalesces steps ?? maxSteps.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads agent definitions from {agent,agents}/**/*.md under a directory, deriving names from paths, using the markdown body as the prompt, reporting parse failures as session error bus events, and validating each entry through the agent Effect Schema.

nodes.name: loadMode
nodes.summary: Loads deprecated mode definitions from {mode,modes}/*.md, validating them with the agent schema and forcing mode: 'primary' on each surviving entry.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads user command definitions from {command,commands}/**/*.md, deriving entry names from directory roots, using the trimmed markdown body as the template, and throwing InvalidError with zod issues on validation failure.

nodes.name: normalizeLoadedConfig
nodes.summary: Strips deprecated theme/keybinds/tui keys from a loaded config object and warns that those settings moved to tui.json.

nodes.name: substituteWellKnownRemoteConfig
nodes.summary: Resolves ${...} config variables inside a remote_config pointer's URL and each header value fetched from .well-known/opencode endpoints, returning the substituted url/headers pair.

nodes.name: patchJsonc
nodes.summary: Recursively applies a JSON patch to JSONC text using jsonc-parser modify/applyEdits, preserving comments and formatting while updating nested keys.

nodes.name: systemManagedConfigDir
nodes.summary: Returns the platform-specific managed config directory (/Library/Application Support/opencode on macOS, ProgramData\opencode on Windows, /etc/opencode elsewhere).

nodes.name: parseManagedPlist
nodes.summary: Parses a managed plist JSON payload and strips MDM-injected metadata keys (PayloadDisplayName, PayloadIdentifier, _manualProfile, etc.) before the payload is treated as opencode config.

nodes.name: readManagedPreferences
nodes.summary: Reads macOS MDM managed preferences for the ai.opencode.managed domain from per-user or system-wide Managed Preferences paths, converting plists to JSON via plutil and returning the config text with its mobileconfig source.

nodes.name: fallbackSanitization
nodes.summary: Repairs invalid YAML frontmatter left behind by other coding agents: skips comments, empty lines, and continuations, and rewrites unquoted values containing colons as block scalars so gray-matter can parse the document.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Reads a markdown file from disk and parses its gray-matter frontmatter, retrying with fallbackSanitization on failure and ultimately throwing FrontmatterError with a descriptive message.

nodes.name: jsonc
nodes.summary: Parses JSONC text (trailing commas allowed) and throws JsonError with line/column, the offending source line, and a caret pointer for each syntax error.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Validates unknown data against a zod schema via safeParse, returning the parsed value or throwing InvalidError carrying the zod issues.

nodes.name: effectSchema
nodes.summary: Validates data against an Effect Schema: first rejects unknown top-level keys with unrecognized_keys issues, then decodes and converts schema errors into InvalidError with standard-schema-v1-formatted issues.

nodes.name: configEntryNameFromPath
nodes.summary: Computes a config entry name by slicing the normalized path after the first matching search root (falling back to the basename) and stripping the file extension.

nodes.name: ConsoleState
nodes.summary: Effect Schema.Class for console-derived config state: console-managed provider IDs, an optional active org name, and a switchable org count, with a derived static zod schema.

nodes.name: requiresExtensionsForCustomServers
nodes.summary: Custom schema filter enforcing that non-builtin LSP server entries declare an extensions array, exempting builtin server IDs and explicitly disabled entries.

nodes.name: paths.ts
nodes.summary: Config file discovery helpers: walks up from a directory to find opencode.json/jsonc config files, and computes the ordered, deduplicated list of config directories (global config path, per-level .opencode dirs, home directory, OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR override) used during config resolution.

nodes.name: files
nodes.summary: Effect generator that walks upward from a directory collecting `<name>.jsonc`/`<name>.json` config files until the worktree root, returned nearest-last so callers can merge in priority order.

nodes.name: directories
nodes.summary: Computes the deduplicated config directory list: the global config path, `.opencode` dirs found between the project directory and worktree root (unless project config is disabled), the home `.opencode` dir, and the OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR flag override.

nodes.name: permission.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the permission config schema: Action/Object/Rule schemas plus the Info transform that normalizes the shorthand action form (e.g. `"ask"`) into per-target rule objects (`{ "*": "ask" }`), exposing a derived zod schema for runtime config parsing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Effect Schema decodeTo with SchemaGetter transforms; known permission keys (read, edit, bash, task, ...) get explicit struct fields while Schema.StructWithRest keeps arbitrary tool keys valid.

nodes.name: plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Plugin config helpers: discovers plugin files under `plugin(s)/` directories, resolves path-like plugin specs relative to the config file that declared them, and deduplicates merged plugin origins by load identity (npm package name or exact file URL) while preserving provenance.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Scans a directory for `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}` files (including dotfiles and symlinks) and returns them as file:// URL specs ready for dynamic import.

nodes.name: resolvePluginSpec
nodes.summary: Rewrites path-like plugin specs into absolute file:// URLs resolved against the declaring config file's directory (handling file://, absolute, and Windows drive paths), so later config merges cannot reinterpret relative paths against a different base.

nodes.name: deduplicatePluginOrigins
nodes.summary: Deduplicates merged plugin origins by load identity — package name for npm specs, exact file URL for local specs — with last-declared winning, while keeping the full Origin so downstream code knows which config file won.

nodes.name: provider.ts
nodes.summary: Effect Schema definitions for the `provider` config key: `Model` covers per-model capabilities, cost, context limits, modalities, and variant overrides, while `Info` covers provider-level options (apiKey, baseURL, enterpriseUrl, total vs SSE-chunk timeouts) and the provider's model map. Both carry derived zod schemas.

nodes.name: reference.ts
nodes.summary: Schema for the `reference` config key: a record of named entries that are either plain strings, git repository refs (with optional branch), or local directory paths, consumed when cloning reference material for context.

nodes.name: search.ts
nodes.summary: Schema for the `search` config key: `EmbeddingInfo` selects the embedding provider (local xenova/transformers on CPU or the OpenAI API) with model id, dimension, and API key; `SearchInfo` nests it for semantic search configuration.

nodes.name: server.ts
nodes.summary: Schema for the `server` config key controlling the HTTP server: port, hostname, mDNS service discovery toggles, custom mDNS domain, and additional allowed CORS origins.

nodes.name: skills.ts
nodes.summary: Schema for the `skills` config key: additional skill folder paths, remote skill URLs to fetch from, and semantic auto-match settings (injection count and cosine-similarity threshold) for automatic skill context injection.

nodes.name: variable.ts
nodes.summary: Config text interpolation: expands `{env:VAR}` environment substitutions and inline `{file:path}` references (skipping `//`-commented lines, supporting `~/` paths) by reading file contents as JSON-escaped strings, with configurable missing-file behavior.

nodes.name: substitute
nodes.summary: Applies `{env:VAR}` and `{file:path}` substitutions to raw config text: env vars expand inline, file tokens resolve relative to the config file's directory (`~/` aware) and are injected JSON-string-escaped, and missing files either throw InvalidError or expand to empty per the `missing` option.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Workspace adapter registry: resolves workspace types to adapters by combining module-level builtins (worktree) with a project-scoped registration map, so plugins can register custom workspace types per project or globally via ProjectID.global.

nodes.name: getAdapter
nodes.summary: Returns the project-scoped custom adapter for a workspace type, falling back to the builtin registry, and throws for unknown adapter types.

nodes.name: listAdapters
nodes.summary: Projects all registered adapters for a project into WorkspaceAdapterEntry summaries (type, name, description) for listing available workspace types.

nodes.name: registeredAdapters
nodes.summary: Merges builtin adapters with any project-scoped custom registrations, with custom entries overriding builtins of the same type key.

nodes.name: registerAdapter
nodes.summary: Registers a custom workspace adapter scoped to a project ID; pass ProjectID.global to install it for all projects.

nodes.name: worktree.ts
nodes.summary: Built-in workspace adapter implementing git worktree workspaces: configure derives name/branch/directory, create/remove delegate to the Worktree service, list enumerates existing worktrees, and target reports the local directory — all lazily importing the Effect runtime and services to avoid load cycles.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dynamic import() inside a shared loadWorktree() helper so the adapter module stays decoupled from the heavy Effect runtime graph at import time.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Developer guide for the debug workspace plugin: how to register it in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`, run the standalone workspace server script, and how the file-based handshake (port/id written to /tmp and watched by the server) simulates a remote workspace locally, one debug workspace at a time.

nodes.name: debug-workspace-plugin.ts
nodes.summary: Dev-only OpenCode plugin registering a `debug` workspace type that simulates a remote environment: on create it picks a random port, writes the handshake file consumed by the workspace server script, and polls the health endpoint until the fake remote server is up.

nodes.name: waitForHealth
nodes.summary: Polls `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/global/health` every 250ms for up to 30 seconds until the debug workspace server responds OK, throwing on timeout.

nodes.name: writeDebugData
nodes.summary: Atomically writes the debug server handshake file (port, workspace id, env) via temp-file-plus-rename so the watching server script picks up complete data and restarts with the new workspace info.

nodes.name: DebugWorkspacePlugin
nodes.summary: Plugin entry point registering the `debug` workspace adapter: create spins up an external server via the handshake file and waits for health, remove is a no-op, and target routes to `http://localhost:<port>/` as a remote workspace.

nodes.name: schema.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the branded WorkspaceID schema (strings prefixed `wrk`) with an `ascending` static factory that generates sortable, ULID-style workspace identifiers.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Core control-plane type surface: the WorkspaceInfo/WorkspaceListedInfo schemas, the WorkspaceAdapterEntry descriptor, the local-vs-remote Target union, and the WorkspaceAdapter interface (configure/create/list/remove/target) that every workspace type implements.

nodes.name: util.ts
nodes.summary: Provides `waitEvent`, an Effect wrapper around the GlobalBus that suspends until a matching global event arrives, an abort signal fires, or a timeout elapses — the synchronization primitive behind workspace creation and sync fencing.

nodes.name: waitEvent
nodes.summary: Blocks as an Effect until a GlobalBus event matches the predicate, failing on abort signal, timeout, or handler error, with complete listener/timer cleanup wired through Effect.callback's cancellation return.

nodes.name: workspace-context.ts
nodes.summary: AsyncLocalStorage-backed ambient context carrying the current WorkspaceID across async boundaries, with provide/restore wrappers and a safe `workspaceID` getter that returns undefined when called outside any context.

nodes.name: workspace.sql.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle schema for the `workspace` SQLite table: branded WorkspaceID primary key, type/name/branch/directory columns, JSON-encoded extra data, a cascading project foreign key, and a time_used column defaulting to now.
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the repo's snake_case Drizzle field convention so column names never need string overrides.

nodes.name: workspace
nodes.summary: SQLite table persisting registered workspaces: id, type, name, branch, directory, JSON extra payload, owning project (cascade delete), and last-used timestamp.

nodes.name: workspace.ts
nodes.summary: The Workspace control-plane service (~1000 lines): persists workspaces to SQLite, drives the adapter lifecycle (create/remove/list/syncList), maintains remote-workspace SSE sync loops in a FiberMap with exponential-backoff reconnects, replays sync/history events, and implements session warping — moving a session between workspaces by replaying its event log in batches and stealing remote ownership.
nodes.languageNotes: Service methods are Effect.fn generators closed over a shared FiberMap; Schema.TaggedErrorClass errors double as typed wire errors, and the legacy Promise-based adapter calls are bridged back into Effect via EffectBridge.fromPromise.

nodes.name: fromRow
nodes.summary: Maps a WorkspaceTable row into the camelCase Workspace Info shape, including the time_used to timeUsed translation.

nodes.name: synced
nodes.summary: Checks the EventSequenceTable to verify every aggregate in the given per-session sequence state has caught up to its expected seq — the sync fence predicate used by waitForSync.

nodes.name: SyncHttpError
nodes.summary: Tagged error for failed workspace sync HTTP calls, carrying the response status and optional body.

nodes.name: WorkspaceNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Tagged error raised when an operation references a workspace ID that does not exist.

nodes.name: SessionEventsNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Tagged error raised when attempting to warp a session that has no persisted events to replay.

nodes.name: SessionWarpHttpError
nodes.summary: Tagged error for failed session-warp HTTP batch or steal requests, carrying workspace ID, session ID, status, and body.

nodes.name: SyncTimeoutError
nodes.summary: Tagged error thrown when waiting for the sync fence times out, carrying the expected per-aggregate sequence state.

nodes.name: SyncAbortedError
nodes.summary: Tagged error thrown when sync fencing is aborted via signal, wrapping the abort cause as a defect.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Context.Service tag for the Workspace control-plane interface: create, sessionWarp, list, syncList, get, remove, status, isSyncing, waitForSync, and startWorkspaceSyncing.

nodes.name: data-migration.sql.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle schema for the `data_migration` SQLite table that tracks completed data migrations by name and completion timestamp.

nodes.name: data_migration
nodes.summary: SQLite bookkeeping table (name primary key, time_completed) recording which one-off data migrations have already run.

nodes.name: data-migration.ts
nodes.summary: Data-migration runner service: executes registered named migrations inside a forked background fiber, skipping any already recorded in the data_migration table and logging-and-ignoring failures so boot is never blocked; currently ships an empty migration list.
nodes.languageNotes: Migrations run via Effect.forkScoped so they stay resumable until their completion row is written.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Context.Service tag for the DataMigration service, exposing the background migration-runner interface to the rest of the app layer.

nodes.name: app-runtime.ts
nodes.summary: The application's composition root: AppLayer merges ~50 service default layers (config, storage, sessions, providers, MCP, LSP, skills, workspace, worktree, data migration, etc.) over the Instance and Observability layers, and AppRuntime exposes the ManagedRuntime's runSync/runPromise/runFork entry points with run-service attachment pre-applied.
nodes.languageNotes: ManagedRuntime is built with a shared memoMap so layer construction is memoized process-wide; every run* method pipes effects through the attach() wrapper from run-service.

nodes.name: bootstrap-runtime.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal pre-boot runtime that merges only the services needed before the full app layer exists (Config, Plugin, ShareNext, Format, LSP, File, FileWatcher, Vcs, Snapshot, Bus) over the Observability layer.

nodes.name: bridge.ts
nodes.summary: Effect-to-Promise bridge that preserves ambient context: fromPromise runs a JS async callback while reinstalling the legacy Instance/WorkspaceContext AsyncLocalStorage, and make produces a promise/fork/run bridge that re-enters Effect with the captured instance and workspace refs attached.
nodes.languageNotes: Node's AsyncLocalStorage propagates across await boundaries where Effect's InstanceRef/WorkspaceRef do not — the bridge restores ALS before invoking callbacks that may spawn nested Effect runtimes.

nodes.name: fromPromise
nodes.summary: Runs a Promise-returning callback as an Effect while restoring legacy Instance and Workspace AsyncLocalStorage contexts, so nested AppRuntime.runPromise calls inside the callback keep their ambient instance/workspace state.

nodes.name: make
nodes.summary: Builds a Shape bridge (promise/fork/run) that captures the current InstanceRef/WorkspaceRef with an AsyncLocalStorage fallback and re-executes wrapped effects with the original Effect context provided, translating exits back into succeed/failCause.

nodes.name: config-service.ts
nodes.summary: Factory for config-backed Context services: given a service id and a map of Effect Config definitions it generates a typed service class with a `layer` for injecting pre-parsed values (tests) and a `defaultLayer` that parses config once from the active ConfigProvider.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Class factory deriving a Context.Service from a record of Effect Config fields, generating static `layer` (inject parsed values) and `defaultLayer` (parse via Config.all) layers so env names, defaults, and validation stay in one place.

nodes.name: instance-ref.ts
nodes.summary: Defines Effect Context.Reference slots (InstanceRef, WorkspaceRef) for propagating the current project instance context and workspace ID through Effect fibers without explicit parameter passing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Effect 4 Context.Reference with defaultValue factories as a fiber-safe alternative to Node's AsyncLocalStorage.

nodes.name: instance-registry.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny global registry of per-directory disposer callbacks used to invalidate instance-scoped state; disposeInstance runs all registered disposers concurrently and ignores individual failures.

nodes.name: registerDisposer
nodes.summary: Registers a disposer callback and returns an unsubscribe function; disposers receive a directory key so they can invalidate matching instance state.

nodes.name: disposeInstance
nodes.summary: Invokes every registered disposer via Promise.allSettled and waits for all outcomes, tolerating individual disposer errors.

nodes.name: instance-state.ts
nodes.summary: Implements InstanceState, a per-directory scoped cache over Effect's ScopedCache that lazily initializes state for each project instance and invalidates it on dispose — the backbone for instance-scoped services like Env, File, and Format.
nodes.languageNotes: ScopedCache is created with infinite capacity keyed by directory, but lookup ignores the key and derives state from the ambient InstanceRef context instead.

nodes.name: bind
nodes.summary: Wraps a function so it executes with the ambient InstanceContext restored, falling back to the fiber's InstanceRef when Instance.bind throws LocalContext.NotFound.

nodes.name: make
nodes.summary: Creates an InstanceState cache whose lookup runs the init effect with the current instance context, registering a directory-keyed disposer that invalidates the cache entry on dispose.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Yields the cached state value for the current instance directory, initializing it on first access.

nodes.name: use
nodes.summary: Maps the current instance state through a selector function.

nodes.name: useEffect
nodes.summary: Flat-maps the current instance state into an effect that produces a derived value.

nodes.name: has
nodes.summary: Checks whether state has already been initialized for the current directory without triggering a lookup.

nodes.name: invalidate
nodes.summary: Evicts the cached state for the current directory, forcing re-initialization on next access.

nodes.name: run-service.ts
nodes.summary: Runtime helpers that attach InstanceRef/WorkspaceRef context to effects and build a ManagedRuntime whose run* executors automatically re-attach the instance context, letting non-Effect code call services.
nodes.languageNotes: ManagedRuntime runSync/runPromise/runPromiseExit/runFork/runCallback variants are each wrapped so callback-style consumers inherit the ambient instance context.

nodes.name: attachWith
nodes.summary: Provides the given instance and workspace references to an effect via Effect.provideService.

nodes.name: attach
nodes.summary: Captures the current InstanceContext (from Instance.current or the fiber's references) and attaches it to an effect so it runs with the right instance.

nodes.name: makeRuntime
nodes.summary: Builds a ManagedRuntime from a service and layer, returning runSync/runPromise/runPromiseExit/runFork/runCallback executors that attach instance context to every invocation.

nodes.name: runner.ts
nodes.summary: Implements a generic single-flight Runner state machine (Idle/Running/Shell/ShellThenRun) over Effect SynchronizedRef, serializing work so only one effect runs at a time, with exclusive shell mode, interruption recovery, and cancellation semantics.
nodes.languageNotes: SynchronizedRef.modifyEffect makes state transitions atomic; interrupt-only exits are converted to a Cancelled tagged error so callers can distinguish user cancellation from failure.

nodes.name: make
nodes.summary: Runner factory wiring ensureRunning (queue work behind a running fiber), startShell (exclusive shell mode with ready latch, busy error, and onInterrupt recovery), cancel, plus state/busy accessors over an atomic state reference.

nodes.name: service-use.ts
nodes.summary: Provides serviceUse, a Proxy-based accessor that lazily wraps every Effect-returning method of a Context.Service so callers can invoke service methods directly while adding the service identifier to the effect requirements.
nodes.languageNotes: The ServiceUse mapped type filters the service shape to Effect-returning methods only; the Proxy property access is the single dynamic boundary.

nodes.name: serviceUse
nodes.summary: Creates a Proxy whose property access returns a function that runs the corresponding service method inside tag.use, dying with a descriptive error for non-function members.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Env service exposing get/all/set/remove over a per-instance snapshot of process.env backed by InstanceState, so environment mutations are scoped to the current project instance.
nodes.languageNotes: State seeds from a shallow copy of process.env on first use per instance; set/remove mutate the snapshot rather than the real process environment.

nodes.name: ignore.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the built-in file ignore rules (build dirs, VCS metadata, caches, logs, OS artifacts) and a match() predicate supporting extra patterns and whitelist overrides, used by file scanning and watching.

nodes.name: match
nodes.summary: Returns true when a path hits an ignored folder segment or glob pattern, consulting whitelist patterns first and honoring caller-supplied extras.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Core File service: maintains a per-instance scan of project files via ripgrep, exposes list/read/search with fuzzy ranking and hidden-file handling, git-aware modified-file info, and text/binary content encoding with structured patch metadata.
nodes.languageNotes: Global-home scans walk only two directory levels with protected-name filtering, while project scans derive the directory tree from ripgrep's file list.

nodes.name: sortHiddenLast
nodes.summary: Splits listing items into visible and dot-prefixed entries, returning visible ones first unless the caller prefers the raw order.

nodes.name: protected.ts
nodes.summary: Enumerates platform-specific protected directories (macOS TCC areas like Documents, Desktop, Mail and Safari data; Windows user folders) that must never be watched, stated, or scanned, exposed as both name sets and absolute paths.

nodes.name: names
nodes.summary: Returns the platform-specific set of home-directory entry names to skip when scanning (populated on darwin and win32, empty elsewhere).

nodes.name: paths
nodes.summary: Returns absolute protected paths — macOS TCC home and Library directories plus root metadata volumes, or Windows user folders — that must never be watched or stated.

nodes.name: ripgrep.ts
nodes.summary: Ripgrep service: downloads and caches a pinned rg binary per platform (15.1.0), then streams file listings and executes JSON-mode content searches with abort racing, Effect Schema result decoding, and an ASCII tree renderer.
nodes.languageNotes: Search output is decoded from rg's JSON-lines format through a Schema.Union (Begin/Match/End/Summary); Effect.raceFirst against an abort-signal effect cancels pending processes.

nodes.name: filesArgs
nodes.summary: Builds the rg argument vector for file listing from a FilesInput (glob, hidden, follow, maxDepth) plus hidden and exclude defaults.

nodes.name: searchArgs
nodes.summary: Builds the rg argument vector for content search from a SearchInput (pattern, glob, limit, file filters) in JSON output mode.

nodes.name: watcher.ts
nodes.summary: File watcher service over @parcel/watcher native bindings with platform backends (fs-events, inotify, windows), ignoring protected and ignored paths, and publishing file.watcher.updated bus events for add/change/unlink.
nodes.languageNotes: The native binding is loaded lazily by requiring the platform-specific @parcel/watcher-* package; subscriptions carry a 10 second timeout guard.

nodes.name: hasNativeBinding
nodes.summary: Reports whether the platform-native parcel watcher binding loaded successfully.

nodes.name: formatter.ts
nodes.summary: Formatter descriptor registry with 28 formatter definitions (gofmt, prettier, biome, oxfmt, rustfmt, ruff, dart, ormolu, and more), each declaring file extensions and an async enabled() probe that resolves the formatter command line, preferring repo-local binaries over global caches.
nodes.languageNotes: enabled() probes range from simple PATH lookups to package.json dependency scans with findUp; prettier, oxfmt, and biome prefer the repo's own node_modules binary to avoid version-skew format diffs.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Format service: on init merges configured formatters with the built-in registry per instance, probes which formatters are enabled, and exposes file() to run the matching formatter command on a file after edits, logging and tolerating failures.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Git service wrapping the git CLI with hardened -c config overrides, streaming stdout collection with byte caps and truncation flags, and operations for branch, merge-base, status, diff, stats, patch (tracked, untracked, or all), and patch application.
nodes.languageNotes: Every invocation injects config overrides (autocrlf/fsmonitor/quotepath off, longpaths/symlinks on) to normalize behavior across environments; porcelain output is parsed from NUL-separated fields.

nodes.name: local-runner.ts
nodes.summary: Builds a local git runner that spawns git via the Effect child-process spawner, collects stdout/stderr concurrently, and converts spawn failures to a GitResult via a per-caller fallback; behavior is pinned by a dedicated characterization test.

nodes.name: gitRunner
nodes.summary: Returns an Effect.fnUntraced git executor: spawns git with the given args and cwd, drains both output streams concurrently, and falls back to a caller-supplied error mapper on spawn or collection failure.

nodes.name: id.ts
nodes.summary: Monotonic prefixed ID generator (ses_, msg_, prt_, ...) producing 26-character base62 IDs whose lexicographic order matches creation time in the chosen direction, with per-millisecond counters for uniqueness and a timestamp extractor.
nodes.languageNotes: Ascending IDs embed a BigInt-computed timestamp offset so lexicographic sort equals chronological order; a module-level lastTimestamp/counter pair keeps same-millisecond IDs strictly monotonic.

nodes.name: ascending
nodes.summary: Generates an ID whose lexicographic order matches chronological order for the given entity prefix.

nodes.name: descending
nodes.summary: Generates an ID whose lexicographic order is reverse-chronological for the given entity prefix.

nodes.name: generateID
nodes.summary: Validates that a caller-supplied ID matches the expected prefix or creates a fresh ID in the requested ordering direction.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates the prefixed base62 ID: combines a monotonic per-millisecond counter with the timestamp and a random suffix, ordered for ascending or descending lexicographic sort.

nodes.name: timestamp
nodes.summary: Recovers the embedded creation timestamp (epoch milliseconds) from a previously generated ID.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: IDE integration helpers: detects the calling IDE from TERM_PROGRAM and GIT_ASKPASS environment variables, checks whether the extension is already installed, and installs the opencode VS Code extension into supported editors via their CLI.

nodes.name: ide
nodes.summary: Detects which supported IDE launched the process by matching GIT_ASKPASS against known editor names when running inside vscode.

nodes.name: alreadyInstalled
nodes.summary: Returns true when OPENCODE_CALLER indicates the VS Code extension already invoked opencode.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs the sst-dev.opencode extension into the named IDE via its CLI, throwing InstallFailedError on non-zero exit or AlreadyInstalledError when the extension is present.

nodes.name: image.ts
nodes.summary: Image service that normalizes message image parts using the Photon WASM library: enforces base64 size and dimension caps (4.5 MB, 2000x2000), re-encoding through progressively lower JPEG qualities and downscaling until the limits are met.
nodes.languageNotes: Photon is imported lazily and cached; its wasm path is patched onto globalThis so Bun-compiled binaries resolve the embedded file.

nodes.name: PhotonUnavailableError
nodes.summary: Tagged error raised when the Photon WASM image processor cannot be loaded.

nodes.name: InvalidDataUrlError
nodes.summary: Tagged error for image sources that are not base64 data URLs, carrying the offending URL.

nodes.name: DecodeError
nodes.summary: Tagged error raised when Photon fails to decode the image bytes.

nodes.name: SizeError
nodes.summary: Tagged error carrying bytes, dimensions, and configured limits, raised when an image cannot be resized below the configured size caps.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: configures a strict yargs CLI wiring 24 subcommands (run, serve, tui attach, acp, mcp, models, upgrade, ...), initializes logging and process metadata, runs the one-time JSON-to-SQLite migration with a terminal progress bar, and centralizes fatal error formatting.
nodes.languageNotes: Raises EventEmitter.defaultMaxListeners to 100 to absorb AbortSignal.any listener accumulation; an explicit process.exit in the finally block avoids hangs from signal-ignoring MCP subprocesses.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Installation service: detects the install method (curl, npm, brew, scoop, choco, ...), queries the latest release version from the matching registry APIs, compares it with the running version, and performs self-upgrade by re-running the original installer; emits installation update bus events.
nodes.languageNotes: Each install method has its own version-source schema (GitHubRelease, NpmPackage, BrewFormula, ChocoPackage, ScoopManifest) decoded via Effect Schema; HTTP requests run through a transient-read-retry filter.

nodes.name: getReleaseType
nodes.summary: Classifies the semver delta between the current and latest versions as major, minor, or patch.

nodes.name: isPreview
nodes.summary: Returns true when running a non-latest release channel.

nodes.name: isLocal
nodes.summary: Returns true when running an unreleased local build (channel 'local').

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Module notes for the LSP subsystem documenting lifecycle invariants and pitfalls: unbounded per-client diagnostic maps, the dead didClose notification handler, LRU bounds inside notify.open, tsserver memory caps via maxTsServerMemory, broken-server blacklisting, and map-bounding off-by-one conventions.

nodes.name: client.ts
nodes.summary: LSP client factory: builds a JSON-RPC connection over a spawned server process, performs the initialize handshake with capability negotiation, tracks open documents (didOpen/didChange), merges push and pull diagnostics into bounded per-file maps with LRU eviction, and exposes wait-for-diagnostics with timeouts plus shutdown cleanup.
nodes.languageNotes: Diagnostics flow through two paths — server-pushed publishDiagnostics and client-pulled textDocument/diagnostic — merged and deduped; MAX_DIAGNOSTICS=200 caps map growth using a >= MAX eviction that lands exactly on the bound.

nodes.name: dedupeDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Deduplicates diagnostics by JSON-stringified identity, preserving first-occurrence order.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Constructs the full LSP client: message connection over stdio, initialize handshake, notification and request handlers (configuration, dynamic registration, watched files), push/pull diagnostic machinery with debouncing and timeouts, notify open/change/close, touchFile, diagnostics accessors, and shutdown cleanup of all bounded maps.

nodes.name: diagnostic.ts
nodes.summary: Formats LSP diagnostics for agent consumption: pretty() renders severity-tagged line:col messages and report() wraps a file's errors (capped at 20) in a <diagnostics> XML block.

nodes.name: pretty
nodes.summary: Renders a diagnostic as 'SEVERITY [line:col] message' with 1-based positions and a severity map defaulting to ERROR.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Builds the <diagnostics> XML block for a file's severity-1 errors, limiting to 20 entries and appending an overflow suffix.

nodes.name: language.ts
nodes.summary: Static map of roughly 120 file extensions to LSP language identifiers (abap through zig), used to resolve document language IDs when opening files with LSP servers.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure data module: a single exported Record with no logic.

nodes.name: launch.ts
nodes.summary: Wraps Process.spawn for LSP server processes, forcing piped stdin/stdout/stderr and asserting all three streams are available before returning the child.

nodes.name: spawn
nodes.summary: Spawns an LSP server process with piped stdio, accepting either (cmd, args, opts) or (cmd, opts) overload signatures.

nodes.name: lsp.ts
nodes.summary: Effect service (@opencode/LSP) managing LSP client lifecycle: matches servers to files by extension, spawns clients per workspace root with in-flight dedupe and exponential backoff for broken servers, and exposes hover/definition/references/symbols/call-hierarchy queries across all matching clients.
nodes.languageNotes: Effect Context.Service + Layer.effect pattern; per-project state kept in InstanceState; broken-server backoff is exponential (max 30s) with a 5-minute TTL reset.

nodes.name: layer
nodes.summary: Effect layer building the LSP service: merges built-in and config-defined servers, spawns clients per file/root with in-flight dedupe and exponential backoff for failing servers, and proxies LSP requests (hover, definition, references, symbols, call hierarchy) to all matching clients.

nodes.name: server.ts
nodes.summary: Registry of 38 language server definitions (TypeScript, Go, Rust, C#, Java, Kotlin, Python, and more), each declaring file extensions, workspace-root detection, and spawn logic — including auto-download and installation of missing servers into the global bin directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Each server is an exported `Info` const object with a root-finding function and an async spawn(); NearestRoot is a shared factory that walks up the directory tree looking for lockfile markers.

nodes.name: NearestRoot
nodes.summary: Root-finder factory that walks up from a file toward the instance directory looking for marker files such as lockfiles, with optional exclusion patterns that suppress root detection entirely.

nodes.name: venv.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves the Python interpreter path from $VIRTUAL_ENV or common .venv/venv directories under the project root, used by the Python LSP servers (Pyright, Ty).

nodes.name: venvCandidates
nodes.summary: Lists candidate virtualenv directories: $VIRTUAL_ENV, .venv, and venv under the given root.

nodes.name: resolveVenvPython
nodes.summary: Returns the first existing Python binary across venv candidates, handling the Windows Scripts/python.exe layout versus bin/python on Unix.

nodes.name: markdown.d.ts
nodes.summary: Ambient TypeScript declaration allowing .md files to be imported as string content modules.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Developer notes on MCP internals: tool permission keys use the mcp_ prefix, permission patterns derive from tool args rather than always ["*"], and MCP tools are filtered through Permission.disabled().

nodes.name: auth.ts
nodes.summary: Effect service (@opencode/McpAuth) persisting MCP OAuth tokens, client info, code verifiers, and OAuth state to mcp-auth.json with 0600 permissions, providing field-level update helpers and token expiry checks.

nodes.name: layer
nodes.summary: Effect layer implementing the McpAuth service over mcp-auth.json; generic updateField/clearField factories generate the per-field token, client-info, verifier, and state operations.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: The MCP client manager (@opencode/MCP): connects local stdio and remote HTTP/SSE servers with OAuth orchestration, converts MCP tools into AI SDK dynamic tools, and exposes prompts/resources with per-server status tracking and bus events.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges the MCP SDK's own zod version with the workspace zod via tolerant loose-object schemas and boundary casts; remote servers try StreamableHTTP transport first, then SSE fallback.

nodes.name: listTools
nodes.summary: Lists tools from an MCP client with a tolerant retry path that bypasses output-schema validation errors via a raw tools/list request.

nodes.name: convertMcpTool
nodes.summary: Converts an MCP tool definition into an AI SDK dynamicTool with a normalized JSON schema object and a callTool executor using timeout with progress-based reset.

nodes.name: fetchFromClient
nodes.summary: Generic wrapper that lists named items (prompts/resources) from an MCP client and indexes them under sanitized client:name keys, swallowing per-client errors.

nodes.name: layer
nodes.summary: Effect layer for the MCP service: stdio/remote transport creation with StreamableHTTP-then-SSE fallback, OAuth flows via McpOAuthProvider and the local callback server, cached tools/prompts/resources per server, and status-change bus events with TUI toasts for auth requirements.

nodes.name: oauth-callback.ts
nodes.summary: Local HTTP callback server (default port 19876) that receives OAuth redirect codes for MCP authorization, correlating pending flows by state with a 5-minute timeout and browser-friendly success/error pages.

nodes.name: handleRequest
nodes.summary: Handles the OAuth redirect request: validates state against pending auths, resolves or rejects the waiting flow, and renders styled HTML success/error pages.

nodes.name: ensureRunning
nodes.summary: Starts the single shared callback HTTP server if not already listening, rebinding port and path from a custom redirect URI.

nodes.name: waitForCallback
nodes.summary: Registers a pending auth by oauthState and resolves with the authorization code when the redirect arrives, timing out after 5 minutes.

nodes.name: oauth-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the MCP SDK's OAuthClientProvider interface backed by the McpAuth store: supplies client metadata, authorization redirects, token persistence, and PKCE state for remote MCP server authorization.

nodes.name: McpOAuthProvider
nodes.summary: OAuthClientProvider implementation storing tokens, client information, code verifiers, and state through McpAuth; publishes authorization redirects via callback and invalidates stored credentials on auth failure.

nodes.name: parseRedirectUri
nodes.summary: Extracts port and path from a redirect URI for configuring the callback server.

nodes.name: node.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-exporting Node-only entry points (Config, Server, bootstrap, Database, JsonMigration) for consumers that run the full server runtime.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Parses the apply_patch format (Add/Update/Delete File with @@ hunks) and computes new file contents from matched chunks using exact, fuzzy, ambiguity-aware, and backward context search with BOM handling.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure parsing/derivation layer with no filesystem IO — the caller reads original files and writes results; matcher comparators come from tool/matcher.

nodes.name: parsePatchHeader
nodes.summary: Parses *** Add/Delete/Update File headers including Move to and Force Move to directives, returning the file path, move target, force flag, and next line index.

nodes.name: parseUpdateFileChunks
nodes.summary: Parses @@ context-headed hunks with keep/remove/add change lines, rejecting malformed lines and empty hunks while tracking End of File markers.

nodes.name: parseAddFileContent
nodes.summary: Collects the raw content lines of an Add File block until the next *** directive, stripping heredoc fences.

nodes.name: parsePatch
nodes.summary: Top-level parser turning apply_patch text into Hunk[] operations (add, delete, update with optional move) by delegating to the header and chunk parsers.

nodes.name: deriveNewContentsFromChunks
nodes.summary: Applies parsed update chunks to the original file content, producing the new full file text via replacement computation.

nodes.name: computeReplacements
nodes.summary: Locates each chunk's old_lines within the original file using exact, fuzzy, ambiguity-aware, and backward pattern search, resolving the line ranges to replace.

nodes.name: applyReplacements
nodes.summary: Splices computed replacements into the line array in descending order so earlier offsets stay valid.

nodes.name: seekSequence
nodes.summary: Finds a line sequence in the file supporting EOF anchoring, uniqueness requirements, and forward/backward search with comparator-based matching.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Developer notes on the permission engine: disabled() only hides tools on catch-all deny, Wildcard.match is exact glob matching, evaluate() is last-match-wins defaulting to ask, ask() ordering between DB-persisted approvals and config rules, plus known flaky-test caveats.

nodes.name: arity.ts
nodes.summary: Provides command-prefix arity lookup for bash commands: the longest matching prefix wins, so `git checkout main` resolves to the two-token human-readable command used to build permission patterns.
nodes.languageNotes: The ARITY dictionary was LLM-generated from a strict prompt; flags never count as tokens and only subcommands extend the arity.

nodes.name: prefix
nodes.summary: Returns the leading tokens that form the human-readable command, using the longest prefix found in the arity dictionary (falling back to the first token).

nodes.name: evaluate.ts
nodes.summary: Pure permission rule evaluation: flattens rulesets and returns the last rule whose permission and pattern both wildcard-match, defaulting to ask when nothing matches.

nodes.name: evaluate
nodes.summary: Flattens rulesets and returns the last rule matching both permission and pattern via Wildcard.match, defaulting to an ask rule with pattern `*`.

nodes.name: evaluateWithSource
nodes.summary: Same last-match-wins evaluation but tags each flattened rule with its source ruleset label so callers can report where a decision came from.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: The permission engine (@opencode/Permission): ask() evaluates config rules against DB-persisted approvals (deny always wins) and waits on a Deferred with a 5-minute timeout that broadcasts a synthetic reject; reply() resolves prompts, cascades rejects across the session, and transactionally persists 'always allow' rules. Also defines the Action/Rule/Ruleset schemas, tagged error classes, and the disabled() catch-all-deny tool filter.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Effect.raceFirst (not Effect.race) so the timeout branch's failure wins over a still-pending Deferred.await; approved rulesets are snapshot before the DB upsert to stay atomic under cooperative scheduling.

nodes.name: Request
nodes.summary: Effect Schema class for a permission ask: identifiers, session, permission name, patterns, metadata, always-approval patterns, and an optional tool call reference.

nodes.name: layer
nodes.summary: Effect layer implementing ask/reply/list: Deferred-based prompt waiting with a raceFirst timeout that publishes a synthetic Rejected event, session-wide reject cascade, and transactional upsert of always-allow rules into the PermissionTable.

nodes.name: fromConfig
nodes.summary: Converts the config permission map into a flat ruleset, expanding ~ and $HOME prefixes in patterns and treating plain string values as catch-all rules.

nodes.name: disabled
nodes.summary: Computes which tools to hide from the LLM entirely: a tool is disabled only by a catch-all deny pattern that is not overridden by a specific allow/ask rule for that tool.

nodes.name: schema.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the PermissionID branded string newtype (validated to start with 'per') with an ascending ID generator and a zod bridge for SDK boundaries.

nodes.name: PermissionID
nodes.summary: Branded PermissionID newtype built on Effect Schema with a 'per' prefix check, a static ascending() generator, and a zod conversion static.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Plugin runtime guide covering hook execution and isolation, legacy vs v1 plugin format detection, plugin meta tracking, config hooks mutating the config object in place, and Agent.defaultLayer cascading through Plugin.defaultLayer.

nodes.name: azure.ts
nodes.summary: Built-in plugin declaring the Azure API-key auth method, prompting for the resource name when AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME is unset.

nodes.name: AzureAuthPlugin
nodes.summary: Returns hooks declaring the Azure API-key auth method with a conditional resource-name prompt driven by the AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME environment variable.

nodes.name: cloudflare.ts
nodes.summary: Built-in plugins for Cloudflare Workers AI and AI Gateway auth prompts; the gateway plugin also strips maxOutputTokens for OpenAI reasoning models routed through the OpenAI-compatible SDK, which would otherwise reject the field.

nodes.name: CloudflareWorkersAuthPlugin
nodes.summary: Declares the cloudflare-workers-ai API-key auth method with a conditional account ID prompt driven by CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID.

nodes.name: CloudflareAIGatewayAuthPlugin
nodes.summary: Declares gateway auth prompts for account and gateway IDs and rewrites chat params to drop the output token cap for OpenAI reasoning models behind the AI Gateway.

nodes.name: codex.ts
nodes.summary: Codex (ChatGPT) auth plugin implementing the OpenAI OAuth browser flow with PKCE: runs a local callback server on port 1455, exchanges and refreshes tokens, extracts the ChatGPT account ID from JWT claims, and registers the allowed codex models.

nodes.name: parseJwtClaims
nodes.summary: Decodes the payload segment of a JWT into IdTokenClaims, returning undefined for malformed tokens.

nodes.name: extractAccountId
nodes.summary: Extracts the ChatGPT account ID from the id_token JWT claims, falling back to the access_token claims.

nodes.name: startOAuthServer
nodes.summary: Starts the local OAuth callback HTTP server on port 1455 and resolves once the redirect lands with the authorization code and state.

nodes.name: waitForOAuthCallback
nodes.summary: Waits for the OAuth callback with a polling safety margin against clock skew, then exchanges the authorization code for tokens.

nodes.name: CodexAuthPlugin
nodes.summary: Main Codex plugin: wires the auth loader with token refresh and account-ID resolution, registers the allowed codex models with cost limits, and transforms codex request bodies during chat.params.

nodes.name: copilot.ts
nodes.summary: GitHub Copilot auth plugin: device-code login with token exchange and refresh polling, dynamic model listing from the Copilot API (with static fallback), and a fetch wrapper injecting Copilot session tokens plus request intent headers.

nodes.name: CopilotAuthPlugin
nodes.summary: Main Copilot plugin: provider model listing via CopilotModels with enterprise URL support, auth loader performing device-code login and token refresh, and a fetch shim that detects vision/agent intent from request bodies and injects Copilot tokens.

nodes.name: models.ts
nodes.summary: Fetches the Copilot models API and maps entries into SDK Model objects, resolving reasoning/vision capabilities, context limits, and endpoint-specific routing (Anthropic messages API versus the Copilot API).

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Maps one remote Copilot model entry to an SDK Model, choosing the API npm package and URL from supported endpoints and merging limits and capabilities with previously known model data.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Fetches the Copilot models endpoint with auth headers and returns the built model map, falling back to existing models on error.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: The plugin host (@opencode/Plugin): loads built-in auth plugins plus external plugins from configured origins, wires their hooks into an isolated trigger chain, bridges bus events to plugin event hooks, and hands each plugin an SDK client backed by the in-process server.

nodes.name: layer
nodes.summary: Effect layer for the plugin host: initializes built-in and external plugins (skipping externals in pure mode) with an in-process SDK client, isolates hook failures per plugin, forwards bus events to plugin event hooks, and applies config hooks after load.

nodes.name: install.ts
nodes.summary: Installs plugins from npm specs: reads plugin manifests and package metadata to resolve server/tui targets, and patches opencode.json/jsonc config files via structured jsonc edits under file locking, with injectable filesystem dependencies for testing.

nodes.name: patchPluginList
nodes.summary: Rewrites the plugin array in an opencode.json(c) file using structured jsonc edits, inserting or replacing the plugin spec and handling malformed or missing arrays.

nodes.name: installPlugin
nodes.summary: Installs a plugin spec into the global plugin directory via the resolver dependency, returning the install target or a typed install_failed error.

nodes.name: readPluginManifest
nodes.summary: Reads a plugin's package.json to derive server/tui targets from its exports map, bin entries, and the opencode-specific fields.

nodes.name: patchOne
nodes.summary: Patches one config file for a plugin target: validates the JSON, applies edits while holding a flock, and reports add/replace/noop outcomes with structured errors.

nodes.name: patchPluginConfig
nodes.summary: Entry point that patches all relevant config files for a plugin's targets, with injectable read/write/exists/files dependencies for testing.

nodes.name: loader.ts
nodes.summary: PluginLoader namespace implementing the staged plugin loading pipeline: normalize config specs into plans, resolve install/target/entrypoint, check version compatibility, dynamically import the module, and retry file-based plugins once after dependency preparation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a TypeScript namespace (PluginLoader) as the module's public surface, with typed result objects ({ok: true/false, stage}) instead of exceptions for per-stage failure reporting.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: Resolves a planned plugin spec to a concrete entrypoint in three gated stages (install, entry detection, semver compatibility), returning a typed ok/missing/error result so callers can report exactly why a plugin was skipped.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Dynamically imports a resolved plugin entrypoint module, failing softly with a typed error instead of throwing when the import fails or yields an empty module.

nodes.name: attempt
nodes.summary: Runs one candidate through the full resolve/load pipeline, silently skipping deprecated plugins, routing missing-entrypoint results to a separate callback (for theme-only packages), and adapting loaded modules via a caller-supplied finisher.

nodes.name: loadExternal
nodes.summary: Resolves and loads all configured plugins in parallel, retrying failed file-based plugins once after an optional wait() dependency-preparation hook while preserving result order.

nodes.name: meta.ts
nodes.summary: Persistent plugin metadata store (plugin-meta.json) tracking load counts, first/last seen timestamps, fingerprints, and theme files per plugin, guarded by cross-process file locks.

nodes.name: entryCore
nodes.summary: Builds the core metadata fields for a plugin touch record by resolving its file target, modification time, parsed specifier, and npm version.

nodes.name: next
nodes.summary: Merges a new core record into a previous store entry using fingerprints, returning a first/updated/same state plus timestamps and an incremented load count.

nodes.name: touchMany
nodes.summary: Records many plugin loads atomically: acquires a file lock, reads the store, merges each row via fingerprint comparison, and writes the updated JSON back.

nodes.name: touch
nodes.summary: Single-plugin convenience wrapper around touchMany that records one spec/target/id triple.

nodes.name: setTheme
nodes.summary: Attaches or replaces a theme definition on a plugin's store entry under a file lock so the TUI can resolve theme files shipped by plugins.

nodes.name: list
nodes.summary: Lists all plugin metadata entries by reading the store under a shared file lock.

nodes.name: shared.ts
nodes.summary: Shared plugin resolution primitives used by both the loader and metadata store: spec parsing (npm/folder/file URLs), entrypoint detection from package exports, semver compatibility checks, theme extraction, and V1 plugin module reading.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses npm-package-arg (npa) for spec parsing and handles Windows drive-letter absolute paths with a dedicated regex guard alongside path.isAbsolute.

nodes.name: parsePluginSpecifier
nodes.summary: Parses a raw plugin specifier into a structured form (name/version/source), falling back to the raw string when npm-package-arg cannot classify it.

nodes.name: resolvePluginEntrypoint
nodes.summary: Resolves a plugin target to a loadable file URL by consulting package.json exports for the requested kind, then falling back to directory index files and legacy package layouts.

nodes.name: resolvePathPluginTarget
nodes.summary: Resolves file:// and absolute-path plugin specs to on-disk targets, picking an index file when the target is a directory.

nodes.name: resolvePluginTarget
nodes.summary: Resolves a plugin spec to an on-disk target: path specs go through resolvePathPluginTarget, npm specs are installed on demand via Npm.add and located in the plugin cache.

nodes.name: checkPluginCompatibility
nodes.summary: Validates an npm plugin's declared engines/opencode semver range against the running installation version, skipping the gate for malformed or missing declarations.

nodes.name: createPluginEntry
nodes.summary: Creates the base plugin entry (source, target, optional entrypoint and package.json) for a resolved target, the shared building block for loader Resolved/Missing results.

nodes.name: readPackageThemes
nodes.summary: Extracts theme file declarations from a plugin package.json, accepting either an array of paths or a path map, and resolving each against the package root.

nodes.name: readV1Plugin
nodes.summary: Adapts a legacy V1 plugin module (function or config-object form) into the current plugin entry shape, extracting hooks, inits, and auth handlers.

nodes.name: resolvePluginId
nodes.summary: Determines a stable plugin id from an explicit id, module export, or the installed package.json name.

nodes.name: bootstrap-service.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the InstanceBootstrap Context.Service tag and Interface separately from its implementation so InstanceStore can depend on the bootstrap without importing the heavy implementation dependency graph.
nodes.languageNotes: Illustrates the tag/implementation split pattern for Effect services: a lightweight tag file breaks what would otherwise be a circular layer dependency.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Context.Service tag (@opencode/InstanceBootstrap) exposing a single run effect that materializes all per-instance services.

nodes.name: bootstrap.ts
nodes.summary: Instance bootstrap layer that eagerly yields eleven core services (config, file, watcher, format, LSP, plugin, project, reference, share, snapshot, VCS) at layer init, then runs plugin init first followed by concurrent service init on each instance boot.
nodes.languageNotes: Dependences are captured in the Layer generator so the returned run effect has R = never; per-service slow work is delegated to each service's own forkScoped init.

nodes.name: instance-context.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the InstanceContext shape (directory, worktree, project) and the async-local-storage context that carries it, plus containsPath for project-boundary permission checks.

nodes.name: containsPath
nodes.summary: Checks whether a path lies inside the working directory or the enclosing worktree, skipping the worktree check for non-git projects where worktree is '/' so external_directory permissions still apply.

nodes.name: instance-layer.ts
nodes.summary: Compose-only layer that lazily imports the bootstrap implementation at layer construction time and wires InstanceStore.defaultLayer on top of it, keeping the heavy bootstrap graph out of static import order.
nodes.languageNotes: Layer.unwrap + dynamic import defers the bootstrap module graph until the layer is actually built, a common trick to break init-time dependency cycles.

nodes.name: instance-runtime.ts
nodes.summary: Promise-style bridge exposing InstanceStore load/dispose/disposeAll/reload operations to non-Effect callers via AppRuntime.runPromise.

nodes.name: instance-store.ts
nodes.summary: Per-directory instance cache built on Effect Deferreds: concurrent loads share a single boot future, reload swaps the entry after running disposers and emitting server.instance.disposed, and layer finalization disposes all instances.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Effect.uninterruptibleMask with restore() around Deferred.await so callers remain interruptible while cache entry creation is not; disposeAll is memoized via Effect.cachedWithTTL(Duration.zero).

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Context.Service tag (@opencode/InstanceStore) exposing load, reload, dispose, disposeAll, and provide for instance lifecycle management.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Returns the InstanceContext for a directory, deduplicating concurrent loads through a cached Deferred entry that is removed again if boot fails.

nodes.name: reload
nodes.summary: Replaces the cached instance for a directory: waits out the previous load, runs its disposers, emits server.instance.disposed, then boots a fresh instance into a new Deferred entry.

nodes.name: instance.ts
nodes.summary: Instance facade reading directory/worktree/project from the async-local instance context, with bind() to re-capture context for external callbacks and restore() to bridge from Effect's InstanceRef back into sync ALS code.

nodes.name: project.sql.ts
nodes.summary: Drizzle ORM definition of the project table: branded ProjectID primary key, worktree, VCS/icon metadata, JSON sandboxes and commands columns, plus shared timestamps and time_initialized.
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the repo's snake_case field convention so column names never need string overrides; JSON columns use text({ mode: "json" }) with $type<> casts.

nodes.name: project
nodes.summary: SQLite project table storing one row per discovered repository: id (root commit hash or 'global'), worktree, vcs, display metadata, sandboxes list, commands, and lifecycle timestamps.

nodes.name: project.ts
nodes.summary: Project service: derives a stable project identity from the git worktree (root-commit id cached in .git/opencode), upserts rows with sandbox tracking, and exposes list/get/update/initGit/sandboxes operations plus the /init command subscription.
nodes.languageNotes: Project identity uses the sorted first root commit (rev-list --max-parents=0) as ID so linked worktrees share one project; falls back to the 'global' project id when git metadata is unavailable.

nodes.name: fromRow
nodes.summary: Converts a Drizzle project row into the public Project.Info shape, decoding the vcs literal and collapsing nullable icon columns into an optional icon object.

nodes.name: fromDirectory
nodes.summary: Core discovery routine: walks up to .git, resolves worktree vs bare-repo vs sandbox paths, derives or caches the project id, then upserts the row, prunes vanished sandboxes, and reassigns orphaned global sessions to the project.

nodes.name: list
nodes.summary: Lists all known projects from the database mapped through fromRow.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Fetches a single project by id from the database.

nodes.name: setInitialized
nodes.summary: Stamps time_initialized on a project row, marking that the user completed the /init flow for it.

nodes.name: schema.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the branded ProjectID schema with a pre-made 'global' constant and a zod bridge for use at SDK/config boundaries.
nodes.languageNotes: Schema.String.pipe(Schema.brand("ProjectID")) gives a nominal type over string without runtime overhead; withStatics attaches both zod and constants to the schema object.

nodes.name: vcs.ts
nodes.summary: VCS service providing git diff/status/branch tracking with byte-capped patch generation: batches git diff output, splits combined patches per file, degrades oversized patches to empty stubs, and applies patches via diff-wasm with a clean-tree guard.
nodes.languageNotes: Patch generation is budget-aware at two levels (per-file and total MAX_TOTAL_PATCH_BYTES = 10MB); once capped, later files receive emptyPatch stubs so downstream consumers always see a complete file list.

nodes.name: parseQuotedPath
nodes.summary: Decodes a C-style quoted git path (handling octal escapes for non-ASCII filenames) into its raw value.

nodes.name: fileFromGitHeader
nodes.summary: Extracts the affected file path from a 'diff --git' header line, handling quoted paths and rename/copy syntax.

nodes.name: splitGitPatch
nodes.summary: Splits a combined multi-file git patch string back into individual per-file chunks by locating 'diff --git' boundaries.

nodes.name: batchPatches
nodes.summary: Fetches one batched patch for all changed files against a ref and redistributes it into a per-file map, flagging truncation when the batched output exceeds the byte limit.

nodes.name: nativePatch
nodes.summary: Generates a single-file patch directly (tracked via git patch, untracked via patchUntracked), falling back to an empty structured patch when truncated.

nodes.name: patchForItem
nodes.summary: Chooses the patch source for one file: batched output when available, an empty stub when caps were hit, otherwise a native per-file patch.

nodes.name: files
nodes.summary: Assembles the final FileDiff list in sorted order, accumulating patch bytes against the total budget and marking everything after the cap as capped.

nodes.name: diffAgainstRef
nodes.summary: Runs git diff, stats, and status concurrently against a ref, merges untracked files into the list, and produces the batched FileDiff set.

nodes.name: PatchApplyError
nodes.summary: Tagged error (VcsPatchApplyError) raised when a patch cannot be applied because the directory is not a git repo or the working tree is not clean.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Context.Service tag (@opencode/Vcs) exposing init, branch, defaultBranch, diff, and patch-apply operations for the instance directory.

nodes.name: with-instance.ts
nodes.summary: Promise-based helper that loads the instance for a directory through InstanceStore and runs a synchronous callback inside its async-local instance context.

nodes.name: provide
nodes.summary: Loads (or reuses) the instance context for a directory via AppRuntime and invokes the caller's function within that ALS context.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Engineering notes for the provider layer: transform pipeline execution order and per-module quirks, error-message hygiene (never leak raw response bodies), systemPromptDelivery routing, lazy models.dev provider caching, and the HTTP/chunk timeout semantics.

nodes.name: auth.ts
nodes.summary: ProviderAuth service that surfaces provider-specific auth methods (API key prompts and OAuth) declared by plugins, driving the authorize/callback flow with pending OAuth state kept in per-instance state.
nodes.languageNotes: Effect Schema classes (Method, Authorization) carry a static zod bridge via zod(this) so the same definitions validate at both Effect and SDK boundaries.

nodes.name: Method
nodes.summary: Schema.Class describing one provider auth method (oauth or api) with a label and conditional text/select prompts.

nodes.name: Authorization
nodes.summary: Schema.Class describing an OAuth authorization handoff: callback URL, method (auto or code), and user instructions.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Context.Service tag (@opencode/ProviderAuth) exposing methods, authorize, and callback for provider authentication flows.

nodes.name: error.ts
nodes.summary: Provider error normalization: extracts concise human-readable messages from API errors without leaking raw response bodies, detects context-overflow patterns, classifies retryability for OpenAI-style errors, and parses both stream and call errors into structured results.
nodes.languageNotes: Overflow detection is regex-driven across multiple provider message shapes (including a '(no body)' status-code variant); HTML gateway/proxy error pages get dedicated 401/403 guidance text.

nodes.name: message
nodes.summary: Builds the user-facing message for a provider API error, preferring extracted JSON error fields and status-code defaults over the raw response body, with special-cased text for HTML gateway blocks.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Parses an error body as JSON when possible and normalizes common error payload shapes (error string vs {message}/nested error object).

nodes.name: parseStreamError
nodes.summary: Parses errors surfaced mid-stream (SSE chunks, provider-specific envelopes) into a normalized retry/retryAfter/restart shape for the agent loop.

nodes.name: parseAPICallError
nodes.summary: Normalizes an AI SDK APICallError into a structured result with overflow classification and OpenAI retryability heuristics.

nodes.name: model-status.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the CatalogModelStatus (catalog data) and ModelStatus (adds 'active') literal schemas used to annotate model lifecycle state.

nodes.name: model.ts
nodes.summary: Canonical Model schema for the runtime registry: branded ids, api/npm provider info, capabilities (modalities, reasoning, interleaved thinking), cost and limits, status, options, headers, and variant tables.
nodes.languageNotes: A single Schema.Struct annotated with identifier 'Model' and a zod bridge; the exported type is Types.DeepMutable of the inferred schema type.

nodes.name: models.ts
nodes.summary: ModelsDev service: fetches and caches the models.dev provider catalog to disk with a 5-minute freshness window, cross-process Flock locking, a build-time snapshot fallback, and a background hourly refresh.
nodes.languageNotes: populate() resolves disk -> bundled snapshot -> flock-guarded network fetch in order; Effect.cachedInvalidateWithTTL(infinity) memoizes the result and refresh() invalidates under the same lock.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Context.Service tag (@opencode/ModelsDev) exposing get() for the raw provider catalog and refresh(force) to re-fetch it.

nodes.name: populate
nodes.summary: Resolves the models.dev catalog lazily: disk cache first, then the build-time snapshot, then a flock-guarded network fetch that writes the cache file.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.summary: Re-fetches the models.dev catalog when the cache is stale (or force is set), re-checking freshness under the lock and invalidating the memoized result.

nodes.name: provider.ts
nodes.summary: Central provider registry and LLM dispatch: merges models.dev, config, auth, and plugin contributions into the model list; resolves per-provider AI SDK instances (bundled or npm-installed) with custom fetch, HTTP timeout, and SSE chunk-watchdog wrapping; and applies per-provider quirks (Azure regions, Bedrock cross-region, Vertex, Copilot, opencode zen).
nodes.languageNotes: The custom() function is a ~685-line registry of per-provider loader overrides; SDK instances are cached per (model, env) hash and lazily instantiated from BUNDLED_PROVIDERS dynamic imports or on-demand npm installs.

nodes.name: resolveHttpTimeout
nodes.summary: Normalizes the timeout option: false keeps the request unbounded, a positive number is honored verbatim, anything else falls back to the 5-minute default.

nodes.name: resolveChunkTimeout
nodes.summary: Normalizes the SSE chunk watchdog interval with the same false-disables / positive-wins semantics, never returning a non-positive number.

nodes.name: wrapSSE
nodes.summary: Wraps an SSE response body in a ReadableStream that aborts the request when no bytes arrive within the chunk-timeout window, guarding against fully silent hung streams.

nodes.name: custom
nodes.summary: Per-provider custom loader registry (~30 providers): decides autoload and model visibility from auth/env presence, picks the right SDK surface (responses vs chat vs languageModel), and handles Azure, Bedrock cross-region, Vertex, Copilot, opencode zen, Cloudflare AI Gateway, and GCP vertex auth quirks.

nodes.name: toPublicInfo
nodes.summary: Strips a provider Info down to the public surface via a JSON clone and string coercion, hiding internal option maps.

nodes.name: fromModelsDevModel
nodes.summary: Maps one models.dev catalog entry into the runtime Model shape: branded ids, capability flags derived from modality lists, normalized cost structure, and provider transform variants.

nodes.name: fromModelsDevProvider
nodes.summary: Converts a whole models.dev provider entry (models, experimental modes, provider body/headers) into the runtime provider shape, invoked lazily per provider by getDatabaseProvider.

nodes.name: resolveSDK
nodes.summary: Resolves and caches the AI SDK instance for a model: picks the bundled or npm loader from model.api.npm, builds the factory with baseURL/apiKey/headers, and wraps fetch with request logging, HTTP timeout, and the SSE chunk watchdog.

nodes.name: getModel
nodes.summary: Service entry point returning a LanguageModelV3 for a provider/model pair, delegating to custom loader overrides or the resolved SDK instance and failing with ModelNotFoundError.

nodes.name: sort
nodes.summary: Sorts models with a curated priority list (gpt-5, claude-sonnet-4, big-pickle, gemini-3-pro), preferring 'latest' variants, then descending by id.

nodes.name: parseModel
nodes.summary: Splits a 'provider/model' string into branded ProviderID and ModelID parts.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Context.Service tag (@opencode/Provider) exposing the merged model/provider list, model lookup, cost helpers, and language-model resolution.

nodes.name: ModelNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Schema-defined error carrying providerID, modelID, and optional suggestions when a requested model cannot be resolved.

nodes.name: InitError
nodes.summary: Schema-defined error raised when a provider layer fails to initialize.

nodes.name: schema.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the branded ProviderID (with well-known constants for anthropic, openai, google, azure, github-copilot, and more) and ModelID schemas with zod bridges.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Short notice marking the copilot SDK shim as a temporary GitHub Copilot-only compatibility package that should not be edited or applied to other OpenAI-compatible providers.

nodes.name: convert-to-openai-compatible-chat-messages.ts
nodes.summary: Converts AI SDK LanguageModelV3 prompts into the OpenAI-compatible chat format demanded by GitHub Copilot, handling text/image/file parts, tool calls and results, reasoning metadata, and copilot provider options.

nodes.name: convertToOpenAICompatibleChatMessages
nodes.summary: Maps a LanguageModelV3Prompt message-by-message into OpenAICompatibleChatPrompt: system passthrough, user content arrays with image_url/base64 conversion, assistant tool_calls, and tool result messages.

nodes.name: get-response-metadata.ts
nodes.summary: Extracts standardized response metadata (id, modelId, timestamp) from an OpenAI-compatible chat completion response payload for the vendored Copilot SDK.

nodes.name: getResponseMetadata
nodes.summary: Normalizes the id/model/created fields of a chat completion into the AI SDK provider metadata shape, converting the epoch seconds timestamp to a Date.

nodes.name: map-openai-compatible-finish-reason.ts
nodes.summary: Maps OpenAI chat-completions finish_reason strings to the unified AI SDK finish reason vocabulary for the Copilot SDK's chat model.

nodes.name: mapOpenAICompatibleFinishReason
nodes.summary: Translates chat-completions stop reasons (stop, length, content_filter, tool_calls) into the LanguageModelV3 unified finish-reason union, defaulting to "other".

nodes.name: openai-compatible-api-types.ts
nodes.summary: Type-only definitions of the OpenAI-compatible chat completions wire format: message roles, content parts (text/image/file), assistant tool_calls, and streaming chunk shapes with JSON-record extensibility.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an extensible JsonRecord base type so provider-specific metadata can ride along on every message and content part without breaking the core wire types.

nodes.name: openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts
nodes.summary: Core chat-completions LanguageModelV3 implementation for the vendored Copilot SDK: builds request args (tools, provider options, messages), posts JSON to the API, and parses both non-streaming responses and SSE chunk streams including incremental tool-call argument assembly.
nodes.languageNotes: The doStream TransformStream accumulates tool_call fragments in a pendingToolCalls map keyed by index (some providers omit the index) and merges argument deltas before emitting a complete tool-call part; the zod chunk schema also carries Copilot-specific reasoning_text/reasoning_opaque fields.

nodes.name: OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel
nodes.summary: Implements the AI SDK LanguageModelV3 interface over the OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint; getArgs assembles body/options/warnings, doGenerate returns one content array, and doStream pipes SSE through a stateful transform that emits text/tool-call/reasoning deltas and finish metadata.

nodes.name: createOpenAICompatibleChatChunkSchema
nodes.summary: Builds the zod schema used to validate each SSE chunk, parameterized by the provider's error schema and including Copilot-specific reasoning fields and delta-shaped tool_calls.

nodes.name: openai-compatible-chat-options.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the zod-validated openaiCompatibleProviderOptions schema (user, reasoningEffort, textVerbosity, Copilot thinking_budget) accepted by the chat model's provider options.

nodes.name: openai-compatible-metadata-extractor.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the MetadataExtractor interface that lets providers surface provider-specific metadata from complete responses or accumulate it across streaming chunks.

nodes.name: openai-compatible-prepare-tools.ts
nodes.summary: Converts AI SDK tool definitions and toolChoice into the chat-completions tools payload, filtering unsupported tool types and collecting unsupported-tool warnings.

nodes.name: prepareTools
nodes.summary: Maps LanguageModelV3 tool definitions to OpenAI function-tool JSON (name, description, strict-JSON-schema parameters) and translates toolChoice modes, warning on tool types the endpoint cannot represent.

nodes.name: copilot-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Provider factory for the vendored Copilot SDK: createOpenaiCompatible wires baseURL, bearer-auth headers, and a user-agent suffix into chat and responses language model constructors, returning a callable provider with .chat/.responses/.languageModel methods.

nodes.name: createOpenaiCompatible
nodes.summary: Builds an OpenAI-compatible provider instance that normalizes the base URL, merges auth headers, and instantiates OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel or OpenAIResponsesLanguageModel per requested model type.

nodes.name: openai-compatible-error.ts
