nodes.name: comment-hover.ts
nodes.summary: Provides a floating 'add comment' button that tracks the hovered diff line and triggers line-comment selection, synced via a requestAnimationFrame loop.

nodes.name: createHoverCommentUtility
nodes.summary: Creates and wires a floating comment button that follows the hovered diff line, syncing position every animation frame and opening line-comment selection on click or Enter/Space.

nodes.name: commented-lines.ts
nodes.summary: Marks already-commented diff and file lines in the rendered viewer by setting data-comment-selected attributes over the line ranges covered by each comment.

nodes.name: markCommentedDiffLines
nodes.summary: Applies data-comment-selected to the rendered diff rows spanned by each comment range, resolving start/end to unified or split row indices and merging overlapping comment indices.

nodes.name: markCommentedFileLines
nodes.summary: Applies data-comment-selected to whole-file line rows covered by comment ranges, clamping ranges to the file's rendered lines and merging annotation indices.

nodes.name: diff-selection.ts
nodes.summary: Helpers that map DOM positions inside rendered diffs to logical diff line/side indices and normalize browser selections so they snap to whole diff lines.

nodes.name: findDiffSide
nodes.summary: Determines whether a DOM node sits on the before or after side of a split diff by walking up to the nearest side container element.

nodes.name: diffLineIndex
nodes.summary: Parses a diff row's comma-separated line-index attribute into numeric line indices, filtering out non-numeric entries.

nodes.name: diffRowIndex
nodes.summary: Finds the rendered row index for a logical diff line (and side) by querying data-line/data-alt-line attributes and matching the diff side.

nodes.name: fixDiffSelection
nodes.summary: Normalizes a browser selection inside a diff so the anchor/focus collapse to whole line rows, producing a corrected SelectedLineRange for line commenting.

nodes.name: file-find.ts
nodes.summary: Implements in-file find (Ctrl/Cmd+F) for the pierre viewers: scans rendered line text with a TreeWalker, highlights matches via the CSS Custom Highlight API with an overlay fallback, and manages match navigation and shortcuts across multiple find hosts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the CSS Custom Highlight API (::highlight(opencode-find)) when available and falls back to manually positioned overlay rectangles; match state lives in a SolidJS store and hosts are tracked in a module-level Set so one global shortcut listener can route to the active viewer.

nodes.name: installShortcuts
nodes.summary: Installs a one-time global keydown listener that routes Ctrl/Cmd+F (and F3/Enter navigation) to the currently active find host, skipping editable targets.

nodes.name: createFileFind
nodes.summary: Builds a file-find controller for one viewer: lazily scans rendered line text for query matches, drives find-bar state and positioning, applies highlights via the Highlight API or an overlay fallback, keeps overlay rects synced to scroll, and exposes open/close/focus/next.

nodes.name: file-runtime.ts
nodes.summary: Runtime glue for pierre viewer custom elements: locates the shadow-DOM host/root, syncs the color-scheme attribute with system mode, and waits for shadow content to be ready before firing onRendered.

nodes.name: applyViewerScheme
nodes.summary: Propagates the current color-scheme mode onto the pierre viewer host element as a data-color-scheme attribute (removing it for light mode).

nodes.name: observeViewerScheme
nodes.summary: Keeps the viewer host's color-scheme attribute in sync with system dark-mode changes via a media-query listener, disconnecting the monitor when the host disappears.

nodes.name: notifyShadowReady
nodes.summary: Waits until a viewer's shadow DOM content is ready (rAF polling plus a MutationObserver fallback), then fires onReady exactly once — handling already-rendered, late-mounting, and dynamically-mutating roots.

nodes.name: file-selection.ts
nodes.summary: Reads the user's text selection inside a shadow DOM and converts it into logical file/diff line ranges plus a before/after side for line commenting.

nodes.name: findFileLineNumber
nodes.summary: Extracts the whole-file line number for a DOM node from its nearest data-line ancestor element.

nodes.name: findDiffLineNumber
nodes.summary: Extracts before/after diff line numbers for a DOM node from its nearest data-diff-line ancestor element.

nodes.name: readShadowLineSelection
nodes.summary: Reads the current selection inside a shadow root (using getComposedRanges when available), maps anchor/focus nodes to file/diff line numbers and sides, and returns a normalized SelectedLineRange.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the newer Selection.getComposedRanges({ shadowRoots }) API to read selections across shadow boundaries, falling back to window.getSelection().getRangeAt.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Public surface of the @pierre/diffs wrapper: defines DiffProps, a large unsafeCSS block theming the diff shadow DOM with OpenCode design tokens, default diff options, and diff typography style variables.
nodes.languageNotes: unsafeCSS is injected into the @pierre/diffs shadow root; overrides are expressed with modern CSS (color-mix(), light-dark(), relative rgb() syntax) layered over design-token CSS variables, with dark-scheme fixes under :host([data-color-scheme='dark']).

nodes.name: createDefaultOptions
nodes.summary: Builds the default @pierre/diffs FileDiffOptions for OpenCode (OpenCode theme, wrap overflow, bar indicators, 20-line expansion, hidden file header), including the injected unsafeCSS and split-aware word-diff settings.

nodes.name: media.ts
nodes.summary: Decodes media file content for the session review: normalizes MIME types, classifies image/audio/PDF assets by extension, and turns base64 or data-URL values into renderable data URLs or inline SVG text.

nodes.name: dataUrlFromMediaValue
nodes.summary: Converts an SDK media value (data URL, base64 payload, or SVG text) into a renderable data URL, normalizing the MIME type and percent-encoding SVGs when needed.

nodes.name: svgTextFromValue
nodes.summary: Extracts inline SVG markup from a media value by base64-decoding utf8 image/svg+xml content.

nodes.name: selection-bridge.ts
nodes.summary: Bridges raw DOM text selections to line-based comment ranges: formats labels, previews selected source lines, restores selections inside shadow roots, and exposes a gesture bridge for line-number click/drag selection.

nodes.name: lineInSelectedRange
nodes.summary: Checks whether a given line (and side) falls inside a selected range, normalizing inverted start/end and treating a null side as a match.

nodes.name: restoreShadowTextSelection
nodes.summary: Re-applies a DOM range inside a shadow root on the next animation frame so text selections survive re-renders.

nodes.name: createLineNumberSelectionBridge
nodes.summary: Creates a click/drag-to-select bridge over line-number gutters that tracks gesture state, consumes the resulting line range, and resets on mouseup or pointer leave.

nodes.name: virtualizer.ts
nodes.summary: Acquires and caches @pierre/diffs Virtualizer instances for the scroll container of each viewer, sharing one virtualizer per target element with setup and cleanup on acquire/release.

nodes.name: target
nodes.summary: Resolves the scroll container and virtualizer target element for a viewer, preferring the diffs scroller within the closest pierre host and falling back to computed scrollable ancestors.

nodes.name: acquireVirtualizer
nodes.summary: Returns a shared Virtualizer for the viewer's scroll target, setting it up on first acquire and returning a releaser that cleans it up when the last holder releases.

nodes.name: worker.ts
nodes.summary: Lazily creates and caches Shiki worker pools (unified and split styles) for syntax highlighting and word-diffs, sized at 2 workers per pool to bound memory and Safari worker startup cost.
nodes.languageNotes: The worker URL comes from a Vite `?worker&url` import of @pierre/diffs' Shiki worker; pools are module-level singletons keyed by diff style and guarded for SSR.

nodes.name: createPool
nodes.summary: Creates a WorkerPoolManager of two Shiki workers configured with the OpenCode theme and given line-diff type, initializing it eagerly.

nodes.name: getWorkerPool
nodes.summary: Returns the lazily-created worker pool for a diff style (unified or split), cached as module-level singletons and guarded against non-browser environments.

nodes.name: fixtures.ts
nodes.summary: Sample payloads (diff, code, markdown, changes) used as props by Storybook stories for the session-review and code views.

nodes.name: scaffold.tsx
nodes.summary: Storybook scaffolding factory: picks a component export from a module (by name, default, or first capitalized function), wraps it in an ErrorBoundary, and returns a CSF meta plus Basic story.

nodes.name: pick
nodes.summary: Selects a component from a module by explicit name, default export, or first capitalized function, falling back to a 'missing component' placeholder that lists the module's exports.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Builds a Storybook CSF object (meta + Basic story) for the picked component, rendering it via Dynamic inside an ErrorBoundary with a readable error fallback.

nodes.name: color.ts
nodes.summary: Dependency-free color math for the theme engine: hex/RGB/OKLCH conversions with gamut fitting, plus generators that expand seed colors into 12-step, neutral, and alpha scales for light and dark theme variants.
nodes.languageNotes: Scales are generated in the perceptual OKLab/OKLCH space (with sRGB linearization) so lightness steps stay visually even; fitOklch clamps out-of-gamut colors back into sRGB by reducing chroma.

nodes.name: hexToRgb
nodes.summary: Parses 3/4/6/8-digit hex color strings into RGB components, expanding short forms by doubling each digit.

nodes.name: rgbToOklch
nodes.summary: Converts sRGB to OKLCH via linearization and the OKLab transform, returning lightness, chroma, and hue in degrees.

nodes.name: oklchToRgb
nodes.summary: Converts OKLCH back to sRGB through the OKLab matrix, clamping out-of-range channels.

nodes.name: fitOklch
nodes.summary: Fits an OKLCH color into the displayable sRGB gamut by lowering lightness and chroma until the RGB conversion yields in-range channels, preserving hue.

nodes.name: generateScale
nodes.summary: Expands a seed hex color into a 12-step perceptual scale for light or dark themes, tilting lightness/hue/chroma across steps and capping chroma.

nodes.name: generateNeutralScale
nodes.summary: Generates the neutral (gray) scale from neutral and ink seed colors, mixing toward ink for contrast and enforcing monotonic lightness across the 12 steps.

nodes.name: generateAlphaScale
nodes.summary: Derives an alpha-variant scale by blending each step of a base scale toward transparency according to theme mode.

nodes.name: context.tsx
nodes.summary: SolidJS theme context: ThemeProvider/useTheme built on createSimpleContext, holding a reactive store of loaded themes plus persisted theme and color-scheme preferences (localStorage, cross-tab storage events, prefers-color-scheme) and a preview/commit/cancel flow for the theme picker.
nodes.languageNotes: Themes lazy-load via a Vite glob map (./themes/*.json) with in-flight promise dedup; the 'oc-2' theme is bundled as the synchronous default and preview state is stored separately from the committed themeId.

nodes.name: ThemeProvider
nodes.summary: SolidJS context provider (generated by createSimpleContext) whose init builds the reactive theme store, lazy theme loading, persistence and cross-tab sync, and the preview APIs; consumed through the paired useTheme hook.

nodes.name: default-themes.ts
nodes.summary: Re-exports the 38 built-in desktop themes (oc-2, catppuccin, gruvbox, tokyonight, ...) as typed DesktopTheme constants from their JSON files, plus the DEFAULT_THEMES registry.

nodes.name: desktop-theme.schema.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema (draft-07) for OpenCode desktop theme files: requires name, slug id, and light/dark variants, with definitions for HexColor, ColorValue (hex or var(--...) reference), legacy seed colors, and palettes.
nodes.languageNotes: ColorValue accepts either a hex color or a CSS variable reference, which is how themes can defer to runtime design tokens instead of hard-coding every color.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel for the theme runtime: re-exports color math, theme resolution/CSS application, ThemeProvider/useTheme, type definitions, and all built-in themes as the public UI theme API.

nodes.name: loader.ts
nodes.summary: Theme loader that applies DesktopTheme objects to the document by resolving light and dark variants into CSS and injecting it into a managed style element. Tracks the active theme in memory, supports loading themes from URLs, and toggling color-scheme overrides.
nodes.languageNotes: The default theme (oc-2) emits CSS scoped to :root while custom themes use html[data-theme] selectors, with prefers-color-scheme media queries flipping light/dark token sets.

nodes.name: resolve.ts
nodes.summary: Core theme resolution engine: derives the full CSS custom-property token set (backgrounds, surfaces, borders, syntax, markdown, diff colors) from a variant's seed or palette colors. Uses OKLCH color math, 12-step scale generation, alpha blending, and WCAG luminance checks to produce contrast-safe tokens.
nodes.languageNotes: All hue/lightness/chroma math happens in OKLCH perceptual space; an inline WCAG relative-luminance function (sRGB linearization) picks contrast-safe 'on' text colors for tinted surfaces.

nodes.name: theme-css.ts
nodes.summary: Applies a single light-or-dark theme variant to the document as :root CSS, caching non-default theme CSS to localStorage for instant preload on next load. Detects system color-scheme preference and removes the preload style element once live CSS is applied.

nodes.name: theme-glob.ts
nodes.summary: Lazy theme registry built on Vite's import.meta.glob over themes/*.json, exposing memoized theme IDs, a known-themes set, and a display-name map for roughly 40 built-in themes.
nodes.languageNotes: import.meta.glob turns every theme JSON into a lazy dynamic-import chunk; module-level caches (files/ids/known) memoize the registry after first access.

nodes.name: theme-storage.ts
nodes.summary: Safe localStorage wrappers for theme persistence: canonical storage keys, oc-1 to oc-2 theme-id normalization, try/catch-guarded read/write/drop helpers, and a clearThemeCss utility for the cached light/dark CSS blobs.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Type system for the theming model: HexColor/OklchColor primitives, ThemeSeedColors vs ThemePaletteColors inputs, a discriminated ThemeVariant (seeds or palette, never both), DesktopTheme, token categories, and the flat ResolvedTheme token record.
nodes.languageNotes: The seeds/palette mutual exclusion is expressed with a `never`-typed discriminant pair rather than a string literal tag.

nodes.name: sst-env.d.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated SST ambient type declaration that pulls in the project's sst environment types for the ui package. Do not edit by hand.

nodes.name: vite.config.ts
nodes.summary: Vite build config for the shared ui package: SolidJS plugin, dual icons-spritesheet generation (file-type and provider icons into typed component directories), and a custom plugin that fetches provider logo SVGs from models.dev on dev-server start and build start.
nodes.languageNotes: Custom Vite plugin pattern: configureServer and buildStart hooks fire-and-forget an asset sync so provider logos stay fresh in dev and CI without becoming build-blocking steps.

nodes.name: astro.config.mjs
nodes.summary: Astro/Starlight site configuration for the opencode docs and session-share site: 18 locales, Cloudflare SSR adapter with passthrough images, SolidJS integration, toolbeam-docs-theme, overrides for five Starlight components, and a configSchema integration that runs the opencode schema script after build.

nodes.name: config.mjs
nodes.summary: Stage-aware site constants derived from SST_STAGE: production vs staging URLs for the site and auth console, contact email, social-card service, GitHub/Discord links, and header navigation entries.

nodes.name: robots.txt
nodes.summary: Robots directives allowing all crawlers site-wide while disallowing /s/ and /share/ so shared session pages stay out of search indexes.

nodes.name: theme.json
nodes.summary: Public JSON Schema (draft-07) describing the terminal theme.json format: named color defs (hex, ANSI 0-255, or "none") and a theme object covering roughly 40 color roles from primary and text to diff highlights and borders. Served as a static asset so editors can validate user theme files.
nodes.languageNotes: A $ref-referenced colorValue definition is reused across every theme role, keeping the 183-line schema DRY.

nodes.name: Footer.astro
nodes.summary: Starlight footer override rendered only for doc-template pages: edit-on-GitHub link, issue and Discord links from social config, language selector, Anomaly copyright, and last-updated timestamp.

nodes.name: Head.astro
nodes.summary: Starlight head override that computes dynamic OG/Twitter card images for docs pages via the social-cards service (Base64-encoded, length-capped titles) and suppresses those meta tags entirely on session-share pages.

nodes.name: Header.astro
nodes.summary: Starlight header override that swaps in a simplified site header (site title, nav links from config.headerLinks, social icons) for session-share paths while delegating to the toolbeam theme's default header everywhere else.

nodes.name: Hero.astro
nodes.summary: Routing shim for the hero region: renders the custom marketing Lander on the home route and defers to Starlight's default Hero on every other page.

nodes.name: Lander.astro
nodes.summary: Marketing landing page for the home route: i18n'd hero headline, copy-to-clipboard install commands (curl, npm, bun, brew, paru, mise), feature list, product screenshots for TUI/VS Code/GitHub integrations, and GitHub/Discord footer links, backed by roughly 520 lines of scoped CSS.

nodes.name: Share.tsx
nodes.summary: SolidJS session-share view: connects to the share API over WebSocket with reconnect handling, reconciles messages and parts into a reactive store, and renders the transcript with connection status, cost/token/context-usage stats, deep-linkable message anchors, and a hover-aware scroll-to-bottom button. Includes adapters for v1 payloads and shell initialization.
nodes.languageNotes: Idiomatic fine-grained SolidJS: createStore + reconcile structurally diffs WebSocket snapshots instead of replacing state, and an IntersectionObserver sentinel drives near-bottom detection for the scroll button.

nodes.name: SiteTitle.astro
nodes.summary: Starlight site-title override rendering the logo image with light/dark variants and screen-reader handling when the logo replaces the visible title text.

nodes.name: arrows.tsx
nodes.summary: Catalog of 41 exported Heroicons arrow SVG components (outline set): directional arrows, u-turns, trending arrows, arrow-on-square variants, and pointing/transfer pairs, each a 13-line SolidJS component wrapping static SVG paths.

nodes.name: coding.tsx
nodes.summary: Small Heroicons coding-category catalog exporting IconBugAnt, IconCommandLine, and IconCommand as SolidJS SVG components.

nodes.name: communication.tsx
nodes.summary: Heroicons communication catalog: 15 exported SolidJS SVG components covering chat bubbles, envelopes (including a solid variant), paper airplane, and phone icons.

nodes.name: custom.tsx
nodes.summary: Custom (non-Heroicons) brand and mascot icons: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, the OpenCode logo, Meta, Robot, and Brain, exported as SolidJS SVG components.

nodes.name: data.tsx
nodes.summary: Heroicons data-category catalog: 10 exported SolidJS SVG components for bar and pie charts, cloud upload/download, cubes, and server icons.

nodes.name: file.tsx
nodes.summary: Heroicons file-category catalog: 26 exported SolidJS SVG components covering archive boxes, clipboards, code brackets, documents with status decorations, folders, and presentation charts.

nodes.name: applyTheme
nodes.summary: Resolves a theme's light and dark variants, builds the combined CSS via buildThemeCss, injects it into the managed style element, and stamps data-theme on the document root.

nodes.name: buildThemeCss
nodes.summary: Assembles the final stylesheet string: the default oc-2 theme is scoped to :root while custom themes get an html[data-theme] selector, with prefers-color-scheme dark media queries and text-mix-blend-mode tokens for both modes.

nodes.name: loadThemeFromUrl
nodes.summary: Fetches and parses a DesktopTheme JSON document from a URL, throwing on non-OK responses.

nodes.name: getActiveTheme
nodes.summary: Returns the in-memory theme only if its id matches the document's current data-theme attribute, otherwise null.

nodes.name: removeTheme
nodes.summary: Tears down the applied theme: clears the in-memory reference, removes the style element, and deletes the data-theme attribute.

nodes.name: setColorScheme
nodes.summary: Overrides the document's color-scheme inline style for light/dark, or removes the override to fall back to auto (system preference).

nodes.name: resolveThemeVariant
nodes.summary: The heart of the theming engine: a ~450-line function that turns a theme variant's seed or palette colors into the complete token set. Generates 12-step OKLCH scales per hue, neutral alpha scales, alpha-blended surfaces and borders, WCAG-contrast-checked 'on' text colors, syntax/markdown/diff palettes, and passes through explicit overrides.

nodes.name: getColors
nodes.summary: Validates that a variant defines exactly one of palette or seeds (throwing on both or neither) and normalizes either input into the internal ThemeColors shape with defaults like accent from info and interactive from primary.

nodes.name: resolveTheme
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper resolving a full DesktopTheme into its light and dark token pairs in one call.

nodes.name: themeToCss
nodes.summary: Serializes a resolved token record into CSS custom-property declarations of the form `--key: value;` joined for direct style-element injection.

nodes.name: applyThemeCss
nodes.summary: Resolves a single variant for the given mode, caches its CSS to localStorage for non-default themes, removes the preload style element, and writes the live :root CSS plus data-theme and data-color-scheme attributes.

nodes.name: cacheThemeVariants
nodes.summary: Pre-computes both light and dark variant CSS for a non-default theme and stores them under the theme CSS localStorage keys for fast subsequent loads.

nodes.name: providerIconsPlugin
nodes.summary: Minimal Vite plugin whose configureServer and buildStart hooks kick off fetchProviderIcons fire-and-forget, keeping provider logo assets synchronized during dev and CI builds.

nodes.name: fetchProviderIcons
nodes.summary: Fetches the provider list from the models.dev API (or OPENCODE_MODELS_URL), then downloads each provider's logo SVG in parallel and writes them into src/assets/icons/provider/.

nodes.name: configSchema
nodes.summary: Astro integration that runs the opencode schema generation script (../opencode/script/schema.ts) in the astro:build:done hook to emit dist/config.json and dist/tui.json alongside the built site.

nodes.name: getStatusText
nodes.summary: Maps the connection status tuple (with optional error detail) to the corresponding i18n message string for the share view's status banner.

nodes.name: Share
nodes.summary: Default-exported SolidJS component for live shared sessions: manages a WebSocket with reconnect/status tracking, reconciles incoming message and part snapshots into a store, renders the transcript with part components, cost/token/context statistics, hash-based anchor scrolling, and a hover-aware scroll-to-bottom button.

nodes.name: fromV1
nodes.summary: Adapts v1 share payloads into the MessageV2 store shape: maps AI-SDK-style toolInvocation states (partial-call, call, result) to pending/running/completed statuses, extracts titles, timing, and metadata, and reindexes message parts.

nodes.name: fromShell
nodes.summary: Builds the initial empty share store from shell bootstrap data, seeding session info and a pending user message with current timestamps before the WebSocket delivers real content.

nodes.name: general.tsx
nodes.summary: Largest Heroicons category module for the docs site: 165 auto-generated SolidJS icon components (24x24 outline style) spanning UI glyphs from academic-cap to x-mark, plus hand-authored opencode-specific icons (IconLetter, IconMultiSelect, IconSettings, IconSingleSelect) appended at the end.
nodes.languageNotes: Each icon is a thin SolidJS function component that spreads JSX.SvgSVGAttributes props onto an inline <svg>; because every icon is a named export, consumers tree-shake the catalog down to the glyphs they actually render.

nodes.name: index.tsx
nodes.summary: Barrel file re-exporting all nine Heroicons category modules (general, file, arrows, layout, coding, data, communication, social, media) as the single ../icons import surface used across the web package.
nodes.languageNotes: Header comment marks the catalog as auto-generated by Heroicons category and forbids adding icons directly to the barrel.

nodes.name: layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Heroicons layout category: 13 SolidJS icon components for list and grid metaphors (bars variants, bullet list, table cells, view columns, 2x2 squares) used across the docs UI.

nodes.name: media.tsx
nodes.summary: Heroicons media category: 15 SolidJS icon components covering playback controls (play, pause, stop), cameras, microphone, musical note, and speaker states.

nodes.name: social.tsx
nodes.summary: Heroicons social category: 11 SolidJS icon components for users, user groups, faces, heart, star, and the share glyph used by the session-share UI.

nodes.name: share.module.css
nodes.summary: CSS module styling the root session-share view (consumed by Share.tsx): header with stats and model chips, terminal chrome, tool cards at three responsive width tiers, copy anchors, tooltips, and markdown bodies — all keyed by data-component/data-slot attribute selectors.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CSS nesting with attribute-based selectors (data-component, data-slot) rather than class names, plus a base64 data-URI terminal traffic-light icon and mobile breakpoints at 30rem.

nodes.name: common.tsx
nodes.summary: Shared primitives for the share view: the ShareI18nProvider context that every share component requires, plus locale-aware Intl formatters (number, currency, duration), ResizeObserver-based overflow detection, and the AnchorIcon copy-link component.

nodes.name: content-bash.tsx
nodes.summary: Renders a bash tool call in the share view: command and console output syntax-highlighted with dual-theme Shiki, sanitized via DOMPurify, with a collapsible overflow region for long output.

nodes.name: content-code.tsx
nodes.summary: Minimal Shiki code renderer for the share view: dual-theme (github-light/github-dark) highlighting of a code string with graceful fallback to plain text when the requested language is not bundled.

nodes.name: content-diff.tsx
nodes.summary: Side-by-side diff renderer for the share view: parses unified patches via the workspace @opencode-ai/diff-wasm package, pairs consecutive removals with additions into modified/added/removed rows for the desktop two-column layout, and regroups them into stacked blocks for mobile, highlighting each line through ContentCode.
nodes.languageNotes: Removals and additions are paired index-by-index so a line replacement renders as a single two-column row instead of separate minus/plus rows — a deliberate deviation from raw unified-diff layout, with a look-ahead loop over hunk lines.

nodes.name: content-error.tsx
nodes.summary: Collapsible error panel for the share view that clamps overflowing error output behind a localized show more / show less toggle that appears only when content actually overflows.

nodes.name: content-markdown.tsx
nodes.summary: Markdown renderer for the share view: a configured marked instance with a Shiki highlighter extension (dual github themes) and target=_blank link rewriting, output sanitized with DOMPurify and wrapped with overflow collapsing plus a copy button.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses marked.use() with markedShiki to highlight fenced code blocks inside the markdown pipeline; a custom link renderer rewrites every anchor to open safely in a new tab before DOMPurify sanitization.

nodes.name: content-text.tsx
nodes.summary: Plain-text renderer for the share view with overflow-based collapse/expand and a copy-to-clipboard button; used for user messages and raw tool output.

nodes.name: IconLetter
nodes.summary: Hand-authored opencode icon of a letter glyph, appended after the auto-generated Heroicons set for use in the docs UI.

nodes.name: IconMultiSelect
nodes.summary: Hand-authored opencode multi-select list icon used to represent multiple-choice UI affordances in the docs.

nodes.name: IconSettings
nodes.summary: Hand-authored opencode settings (sliders) icon, a multi-path custom glyph distinct from the Heroicons adjustments icons.

nodes.name: IconSingleSelect
nodes.summary: Hand-authored opencode single-select list icon, the counterpart to IconMultiSelect.

nodes.name: ShareI18nProvider
nodes.summary: Provides the localized share-view message map to all descendant components via SolidJS context; required by every component that calls useShareMessages.

nodes.name: useShareMessages
nodes.summary: Context accessor returning the share UI string map; throws a descriptive error when ShareI18nProvider is missing from the component tree.

nodes.name: AnchorIcon
nodes.summary: Renders a heading anchor that copies the full page URL plus fragment hash to the clipboard on click, swapping to a check icon and tooltip for three seconds to confirm.

nodes.name: createOverflow
nodes.summary: Factory returning an overflow detector: a ref callback that compares scrollHeight to clientHeight through a ResizeObserver, exposing a reactive status signal that drives show more / show less toggles across the share content components.

nodes.name: formatDuration
nodes.summary: Formats milliseconds as a locale-aware narrow unit string (minutes, seconds, or milliseconds) using Intl.NumberFormat unit styling with tiered rounding.

nodes.name: ContentBash
nodes.summary: Highlights the bash command and console output with dual-theme Shiki, sanitizes the resulting HTML with DOMPurify, and collapses overflowing output behind a localized expand toggle.

nodes.name: ContentCode
nodes.summary: Async Shiki highlighter for a single code string via createResource, falling back to plain text when the language is not among Shiki's bundled languages.

nodes.name: ContentDiff
nodes.summary: Transforms a unified patch into paired two-column diff rows for desktop and grouped added/removed blocks for mobile, highlighting every line through ContentCode; pairs consecutive removals with additions so replacements render as single modified rows.

nodes.name: ContentError
nodes.summary: Wraps arbitrary error children in a clamped container that reveals a localized expand toggle only when the content overflows.

nodes.name: ContentMarkdown
nodes.summary: Parses markdown into sanitized, Shiki-highlighted HTML via createResource and adds overflow collapsing plus a copy button; a strip helper unwraps a single outer tag pair before parsing.

nodes.name: ContentText
nodes.summary: Renders preformatted text with an overflow-aware expand toggle and a copy-to-clipboard button; supports a compact variant for tool output.

nodes.name: copy-button.tsx
nodes.summary: Clipboard copy button for the share view that swaps to a check icon for two seconds after copying, with localized aria-labels and tooltips drawn from the share i18n context.

nodes.name: part.tsx
nodes.summary: Core renderer for a single message part in the share view: dispatches on part type and tool name to dedicated tool cards (grep, glob, list, read, write, edit, bash, todowrite, webfetch, task, plus a generic fallback), decorates each part with a copy-link anchor and role/provider icon, and appends footers with locale-aware timestamps and durations.
nodes.languageNotes: A single SolidJS <Switch> over (role, part.type, tool) triples acts as the dispatch table; ProviderIcon guesses the vendor purely from the model ID string via regex, and typed MessageV2 part shapes come from the opencode package itself.

nodes.name: content.config.ts
nodes.summary: Astro content collections configuration: registers the Starlight docs loader and an i18n collection whose schema is extended with every key from en.json so custom share.* UI strings typecheck across all locales.
nodes.languageNotes: Derives the schema extension programmatically — Object.fromEntries over en.json keys — so adding a UI string to en.json automatically widens the i18n schema, with z.string() catchall for locales that are not yet fully translated.

nodes.name: locales.ts
nodes.summary: Locale tables and matching logic for the docs site: the 17 supported docs locales, an alias map (en maps to root, zh to zh-cn, pt to pt-br, and so on), and exactLocale/matchLocale resolvers used by the middleware for cookie and Accept-Language negotiation.

nodes.name: middleware.ts
nodes.summary: Astro middleware handling docs locale routing: canonicalizes /docs/<locale> aliases with redirects, and on bare /docs visits redirects to the locale taken from the oc_locale cookie or the q-value-sorted Accept-Language header, persisting the choice as a one-year cookie.

nodes.name: [...slug].md.ts
nodes.summary: Astro API route serving any docs page as raw markdown text: looks the slug up in the docs collection and returns the body with a text/plain content type, or a localized 404 status when the slug is unknown.

nodes.name: [id].astro
nodes.summary: Session share page: server-side fetches share data by id from the configured API, assembles roughly 45 localized share.* UI strings, builds a dynamic Open Graph social-card URL from the Base64 title, models, and version, and mounts the SolidJS Share view client-only inside a chrome-less Starlight splash layout with noindex meta.
nodes.languageNotes: All i18n resolution happens in the Astro frontmatter before hydration — the messages object is serialized into the client-only Share component, so the SolidJS tree needs no locale logic of its own.

nodes.name: custom.css
nodes.summary: Global stylesheet layering the opencode brand on Starlight: HSL design tokens for backgrounds, text, borders, and interactive states with prefers-color-scheme dark variants, plus targeted overrides for the header, search button, sidebars, social icons, asides, tabs, and expressive-code frames.
nodes.languageNotes: Dual token systems coexist: --sl-* variables override Starlight's theme while --color-* variables feed the share component, unified through prefers-color-scheme media queries rather than a class-based dark toggle.

nodes.name: lang-map.d.ts
nodes.summary: Ambient module declaration giving the untyped lang-map package a typed surface: map(), map.languages(), and map.extensions() are used by the share view to map file extensions to Shiki language names.

nodes.name: starlight-virtual.d.ts
nodes.summary: Ambient declaration for Astro's virtual:starlight/user-images module, typing the optional light and dark logo assets injected by the Starlight integration at build time.

nodes.name: sst-env.d.ts
nodes.summary: SST-generated ambient environment types reference for the web package; auto-generated by the deployment toolchain and not edited directly.

nodes.name: @npmcli%2Fagent@4.0.0.patch
nodes.summary: Bun patch for @npmcli/agent@4.0.0 serializing the proxy getter to a string (this.#proxy.toString()) so the agent returns a plain URL option object instead of a URL instance.
nodes.languageNotes: Bun patch files are named with the package name URL-encoded (%2F for the scope slash) and applied via the patchedDependencies map in the root package.json.

nodes.name: CopyButton
nodes.summary: Clipboard button that writes the given text on click and flips to a check icon with a localized copied label for two seconds.

nodes.name: Part
nodes.summary: Renders one message part: chooses the decoration icon via a Switch over role/part-type/tool, delegates the body to ContentText/ContentMarkdown or a dedicated tool card, and appends duration and localized timestamp footers for the final part.

nodes.name: stripWorkingDirectory
nodes.summary: Strips the session working directory prefix from absolute file paths so tool cards display workspace-relative paths; returns an empty string when the path equals the working directory.

nodes.name: getShikiLang
nodes.summary: Maps a filename extension to a Shiki language name via the lang-map package, with a shellscript override for .conf files and a plaintext fallback.

nodes.name: getDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Converts severity-1 LSP diagnostics recorded for a file into labeled line:column error rows shown beneath Write and Edit tool results.

nodes.name: formatErrorString
nodes.summary: Splits a leading 'Error: ' prefix into a red label plus message, or renders the raw string dimmed when no prefix is present.

nodes.name: TodoWriteTool
nodes.summary: Renders the todo plan as a status-sorted list (in-progress first, cancelled last) with priority markers and a creating/updating/completing label derived from the aggregate todo states.

nodes.name: GrepTool
nodes.summary: Grep tool card showing the searched pattern and either a collapsible match output labeled with a localized N-matches count or dimmed raw output.

nodes.name: ListTool
nodes.summary: Directory listing card that strips the working directory from the displayed path and collapses the output behind a results toggle.

nodes.name: WebFetchTool
nodes.summary: Fetch tool card showing the requested URL with either a formatted error or a collapsible syntax-highlighted response body honoring the requested format language.

nodes.name: ReadTool
nodes.summary: Read tool card showing the workspace-relative path and either an error, the syntax-highlighted file preview from tool metadata, or the raw output.

nodes.name: WriteTool
nodes.summary: Write tool card showing the target path, any severity-1 diagnostics the write produced, and a collapsible syntax-highlighted view of the written contents.

nodes.name: EditTool
nodes.summary: Edit tool card showing the target path with a two-column ContentDiff of the change and any diagnostics the edit produced rendered after the diff.

nodes.name: BashTool
nodes.summary: Thin adapter that delegates to ContentBash with the command, the stdout from tool metadata, and the description.

nodes.name: GlobTool
nodes.summary: Glob tool card showing the quoted pattern and a collapsible N-results output, or dimmed raw output when no count metadata is present.

nodes.name: ResultsButton
nodes.summary: Toggle button that shows and hides nested tool output with a rotating chevron and customizable show/hide labels falling back to localized defaults.

nodes.name: TaskTool
nodes.summary: Subagent task card showing the task description and quoted prompt with the markdown output collapsed behind a show-output toggle.

nodes.name: FallbackTool
nodes.summary: Generic renderer for unrecognized tools: lists the flattened input arguments as a key/value grid and collapses the raw output behind a results toggle.

nodes.name: flattenToolArgs
nodes.summary: Recursively flattens nested tool input objects and arrays into dotted and indexed [path, value] pairs (a.b.c, d[0].e) for the fallback tool's argument grid.

nodes.name: getProvider
nodes.summary: Guesses the model vendor (anthropic, openai, gemini, meta, or any) from a model ID string via a chain of regex tests, used to pick the provider logo.

nodes.name: ProviderIcon
nodes.summary: Renders the vendor logo (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Meta) matching a model ID, falling back to a sparkles icon for unknown providers.

nodes.name: exactLocale
nodes.summary: Resolves an exact, alias-aware locale string to a supported docs locale (URL-decoded and lowercased), or null when the value is not a known alias.

nodes.name: matchLocale
nodes.summary: Fuzzy locale matcher used for cookies and Accept-Language: special-cases Chinese script/region variants, falls back pt to pt-br and no/nn/nb to nb, then tries two-letter prefix matching before giving up.

nodes.name: onRequest
nodes.summary: Entry middleware: canonicalizes /docs locale aliases via redirect and, on bare /docs visits, redirects to the locale from the oc_locale cookie or Accept-Language header.

nodes.name: docsAlias
nodes.summary: Detects /docs/<segment> paths whose segment is an exact locale and computes the canonical redirect target, mapping the root locale to the bare /docs prefix.

nodes.name: redirect
nodes.summary: Builds a 302 response to the given path, optionally setting a one-year oc_locale cookie so the chosen locale persists across visits.

nodes.name: localeFromCookie
nodes.summary: Extracts and fuzzy-matches the oc_locale value from a raw cookie header, returning null when the cookie is absent.

nodes.name: localeFromAcceptLanguage
nodes.summary: Parses the Accept-Language header, sorts entries by q-value, and returns the first language that matches a supported locale, defaulting to root.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Serves a docs collection entry's raw markdown body as text/plain, or responds with a localized 404 status and body when the slug is unknown.

nodes.name: @silvia-odwyer%2Fphoton-node@0.3.4.patch
nodes.summary: Bun patch for photon-node 0.3.4 that lets opencode's compiled binary redirect the image-processing WASM asset via globalThis.__OPENCODE_PHOTON_WASM_PATH instead of the module-relative path.
nodes.languageNotes: Bun patchedDependencies apply unified diffs to node_modules at install time; this one patches the wasm-bindgen loader to accept an injected path.

nodes.name: @standard-community%2Fstandard-openapi@0.2.9.patch
nodes.summary: Bun patch for standard-openapi 0.2.9 making convertToOpenAPISchema tolerate external URL $refs by falling back to the remaining schema properties or a plain string type.

nodes.name: install-korean-ime-fix.sh
nodes.summary: User-facing installer that clones the patched opencode fork and builds a binary fixing Korean/CJK IME last-character truncation on Enter in Kitty and other terminals (issue #14371).

nodes.name: solid-js@1.9.10.patch
nodes.summary: Bun patch applying the upstream Solid.js fix #2046 so the first computation during a transition also sets the committed signal value, replicated across all four dist bundles (dev/prod, ESM/CJS).
nodes.languageNotes: The same two-line runComputation fix is duplicated in dist/dev.js, dist/dev.cjs, dist/solid.js and dist/solid.cjs because the package ships prebuilt bundles.

nodes.name: beta.ts
nodes.summary: Beta-branch merge orchestrator that lists PRs labeled beta, merges them sequentially into the beta branch, and delegates conflict resolution to an AI agent (opencode run with gpt-5.3-codex) before validating with typecheck and the single-file compiled build.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Bun's tagged-template shell ($`...`) for subprocess control, and verifies pushes by comparing git tree hashes of beta against origin/dev rather than trusting exit codes.

nodes.name: commentOnPR
nodes.summary: Posts a formatted failure comment on a PR via gh pr comment explaining why it was excluded from or failed during the beta merge batch.

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: Aborts any in-progress merge and hard-resets the local beta branch back to origin/beta before retrying a PR merge.

nodes.name: typecheck
nodes.summary: Runs bun typecheck inside packages/opencode, returning whether it succeeded while streaming its output.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Runs the self-contained single-file compiled build (script/build.ts --single) in packages/opencode as a beta-branch smoke gate.

nodes.name: commitSmokeChanges
nodes.summary: Commits any working-tree changes left behind by agent-driven fixes during smoke validation, then re-runs typecheck and build to confirm the committed state is clean.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Regenerates dependency state by removing bun.lock and node_modules then running bun install, used when bun.lock conflicts must not be hand-merged.

nodes.name: fix
nodes.summary: Builds a detailed conflict-resolution prompt (merged/pending PR context, bun.lock and deletion rules, typecheck instructions) and spawns opencode run to resolve the in-progress merge, then verifies no unmerged files remain.

nodes.name: smoke
nodes.summary: Final deterministic smoke gate: runs typecheck and the single-file build after the whole batch, and on failure spawns an agent run instructed to fix merge-caused issues without committing.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full beta batch: fetch open beta-labeled PRs via gh, merge each into beta (routing conflicts to fix/cleanup/commentOnPR), push, verify remote tree hashes, run the smoke gate, and push again if the agent changed anything.

nodes.name: changelog.ts
nodes.summary: CLI wrapper that regenerates UPCOMING_CHANGELOG.md by spawning opencode run --command changelog with from/to/variant arguments, optionally reprinting the result or suppressing output unless the run fails.

nodes.name: check-updates.ts
nodes.summary: Monorepo-wide dependency update scanner: discovers every workspace package.json, filters pinned versions, queries the npm registry for the latest same-major release, and reports or applies (--apply, --apply --install) available minor/patch upgrades.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately skips non-pinned specifiers (catalog:, workspace:, ^, ~, github:, npm:, file:) so only exact-pin dependencies are rewritten.

nodes.name: findPackageJsonFiles
nodes.summary: Recursively collects all package.json files under the repo while skipping node_modules, dist, .git and other noise directories.

nodes.name: fetchLatestVersion
nodes.summary: Fetches a package's dist-tags from the npm registry with a timeout, returning the latest tag or null on failure.

nodes.name: fetchVersionsInRange
nodes.summary: Fetches the full npm version list for a package and returns the newest non-prerelease release within the given major, used to propose safe minor/patch bumps.

nodes.name: dedupe-opentui.ts
nodes.summary: Maintenance script that re-points package-local @opentui symlinks (including inside opentui-spinner's .bun entries) at the root hoisted copies so Bun resolves a single module instance across the workspace.

nodes.name: relink
nodes.summary: Replaces a package-local symlink with a fresh relative symlink targeting the root hoisted copy, skipping silently when no root link exists.

nodes.name: duplicate-pr.ts
nodes.summary: Boots an embedded opencode server via the SDK's createOpencode and prompts the duplicate-pr agent with a message plus an optional attached file, printing the agent's final text response.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI args, assembles text/file prompt parts, creates a session on the embedded server, sends the duplicate-pr agent prompt with a 2-minute timeout, and prints the returned text part.

nodes.name: format.ts
nodes.summary: One-liner developer script that runs Prettier with --ignore-unknown --write across the whole repository.

nodes.name: generate.ts
nodes.summary: SDK regeneration pipeline: runs the sdk/js build script, dumps the openapi.json schema from the dev server, and formats the result via script/format.ts.

nodes.name: close-issues.ts
nodes.summary: GitHub maintenance job that finds issues in anomalyco/opencode with no activity for 60 days and closes them via the REST API, first posting an explanatory comment with reopen guidance.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Posts the stale-issue notice comment and then closes a single issue through the GitHub REST API.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Searches for open issues updated before the 60-day cutoff and invokes close on each one, logging progress.

nodes.name: hooks
nodes.summary: POSIX shell installer that writes a .git/hooks/pre-push hook running bun install (best-effort) followed by bun run typecheck so pushes are blocked on type errors.

nodes.name: publish.ts
nodes.summary: Root release publisher: rewrites the version field in every workspace package.json, rebuilds the SDK, delegates to the per-package publish scripts, then commits/tags/pushes the release, syncs versions back to dev, and un-drafts the GitHub release.

nodes.name: prepareReleaseFiles
nodes.summary: Rewrites the version string in every discovered package.json, then runs bun install and the SDK build script so all artifacts carry the release version.

nodes.name: raw-changelog.ts
nodes.summary: Deterministic changelog generator: pages the GitHub compare API between two refs, classifies commits by product area (Core/TUI/App/SDK/Extensions) from touched paths and conventional-commit type, drops reverted commits, computes first-time contributors, and renders the grouped markdown release notes.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes gh api/git plumbing with pure data shaping; team members (from .github/TEAM_MEMBERS) and bots are excluded from contributor credit.

nodes.name: diff
nodes.summary: Pages through the GitHub compare API between two refs collecting commit shas, author logins, and messages into a flat list.

nodes.name: reverted
nodes.summary: Pairs commits with their later Revert "..." counterparts and removes both from the changelog candidate set.

nodes.name: commits
nodes.summary: Builds the changelog commit list: fetches the compare diff, enriches each commit with product areas inferred from git diff-tree file paths, and filters out reverted commits.

nodes.name: contributors
nodes.summary: Maps external contributor logins to the commits they authored, excluding team members and bot accounts from credit.

nodes.name: published
nodes.summary: Fetches the body of an already-published GitHub release and extracts its contributor-thanks section for reuse.

nodes.name: thanks
nodes.summary: Renders the first-time contributor thanks lines, combining freshly computed contributors with names already credited in previous releases.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Groups commits into area sections and conventional-commit types, then renders the final markdown release notes with compare links and the thanks section.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Tiny bash wrapper that dispatches a release by running gh workflow run publish.yml with a bump type argument (default patch).

nodes.name: sign-windows.ps1
nodes.summary: PowerShell release step that signs Windows binaries with Azure Trusted Signing (TrustedSigning module, RFC3161 timestamping); safely no-ops outside GitHub Actions or when Azure credentials are absent.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a ValueFromRemainingArguments param to accept arbitrary file paths and pins the TrustedSigning module to version 0.5.8 for reproducibility.

nodes.name: stats.ts
nodes.summary: Analytics job that aggregates GitHub release asset downloads and npm download counts for the opencode packages, rewrites the README stats table, and ships the metrics to PostHog.

nodes.name: sendToPostHog
nodes.summary: Posts an analytics event to the PostHog capture endpoint under the download distinct_id, warning instead of failing when no API key is configured.

nodes.name: fetchNpmDownloads
nodes.summary: Queries the npm downloads API over a deliberately over-wide date range and sums the daily download counts for a package.

nodes.name: fetchReleases
nodes.summary: Pages through the GitHub releases API collecting tag names and per-asset download counts, with a small delay between pages to respect rate limits.

nodes.name: calculate
nodes.summary: Sums asset download counts across releases and groups them into per-platform statistics entries.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Parses the existing README stats table, computes week-over-week deltas for GitHub, npm, and total downloads, rewrites the row, commits via git, and emits PostHog events.

nodes.name: upgrade-opentui.ts
nodes.summary: Bumps @opentui/core, @opentui/keymap, and @opentui/solid across every workspace package.json and the root catalog, preserving range prefixes (^, ~, >=) and skipping catalog:/workspace: references.

nodes.name: editDeps
nodes.summary: Rewrites the @opentui dependency entries in a package.json dependencies object, keeping each entry's existing range prefix style.

nodes.name: editCatalog
nodes.summary: Sets the @opentui entries in the root package.json catalog to the exact target version.

nodes.name: version.ts
nodes.summary: CI release bootstrap: emits version/tag/release outputs to GITHUB_OUTPUT and creates a draft GitHub release, generating changelog notes via script/changelog.ts for stable builds or an empty beta draft for preview channels.

nodes.name: project.md
nodes.summary: Design spec draft for running sessions across multiple projects and worktrees, sketching a project-scoped REST API (/project/:projectID/session/...) with message, revert, permission, and file endpoints.

nodes.name: session.md
nodes.summary: V2 spec note justifying removal of the dedicated POST /session/:sessionID/init route, which is only a wrapper around the existing /init command flow, to avoid Session.initialize-style special cases.

nodes.name: todo.md
nodes.summary: V2 architecture roadmap listing eleven workstreams with owners: replacing Hono, a new data mode, agent loop and compaction reworks, plugin API, config/auth/model-database/provider/event redesigns, and hot-reloadability.

nodes.name: sst-env.d.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated SST ambient declarations enumerating every infra resource (Cloudflare Workers, KV, R2 buckets, SolidStart console, secrets) so sst resource references are fully typed in application code.
nodes.languageNotes: Header marks it as machine-generated by SST; it augments the Resource interface inside the 'sst' module declaration and should never be hand-edited.

nodes.name: sst.config.ts
nodes.summary: SST infrastructure entry point: defines the opencode app on Cloudflare with Stripe/PlanetScale/Honeycomb providers, production protect/retain policies, and dynamically imports the app, console, enterprise, and monitoring stacks.

layers.name: CLI & TUI Interfaces
layers.description: User-facing surfaces of the opencode agent: the yargs CLI command tree, the OpenTUI terminal app with its dialogs, themes and keybinds, the headless `run` UI, and the ACP adapter that embeds the agent in editors like Zed.

layers.name: HTTP API Server
layers.description: Effect HttpApi server exposing the 50-endpoint REST surface and SSE event streams (sessions, messages, files, config, providers) with auth, CORS, mDNS discovery, and PTY terminal attach, consumed by the web and desktop clients.

layers.name: Agent Session Core
layers.description: The agent runtime: the SessionPrompt run loop, prompt assembly and compaction, message schemas and projectors, agent definitions, the V2 session API, bus events, config loading, project/worktree management, and the package composition roots.

layers.name: Providers, Tools & Extensions
layers.description: Capability integrations the agent loop draws on: LLM provider adapters and transforms (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, Copilot, models.dev registry), built-in tools (bash, edit, webfetch, grep), permission gating, and the MCP, LSP, skill, plugin, search, auth, and IDE extension systems.

layers.name: Data & Persistence
layers.description: SQLite/Drizzle persistence for the agent: session and message tables, 19 schema migrations, the storage layer, cross-device sync, the data-migration runner, share links, and account state.

layers.name: Web App Client
layers.description: SolidJS web client (packages/app) that drives the agent over the HTTP API: components, pages, the global-sync SSE state engine in context/, i18n, and Vite/Playwright build wiring.

layers.name: Shared UI Library
layers.description: Shared SolidJS component kit (@opencode-ai/ui) used by the web app: 130+ components, theme tokens, Pierre styling, assets and i18n primitives, plus the Storybook workshop that showcases them.

layers.name: Shared Core & SDK
layers.description: Cross-package foundations and public API surface: @opencode-ai/core (Effect-zod bridge, logging, flags), opencode's internal util modules (filesystem, wildcard, file references, formatters), the Rust/WASM diff engine, the generated @opencode-ai/sdk client, and @opencode-ai/plugin types.

layers.name: Documentation & Sites
layers.description: Published documentation: the Astro/Starlight docs and share site (packages/web), the Mintlify API reference (packages/docs), root guides (README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG), per-package AGENTS.md instructions, specs, and the .jules performance log.

layers.name: Infrastructure, CI & Release
layers.description: Build, CI, and delivery plumbing: Bun/Turbo workspace config, SST cloud infrastructure, GitHub Actions workflows and CI containers, release scripts, Dockerfiles, Nix packaging, dependency patches, and the standalone /opencode GitHub Action.

tour.title: Entry Point & Monorepo Map
tour.description: Start where the binary starts: packages/opencode/src/index.ts is a strict yargs CLI wiring 24 subcommands (run, serve, tui, acp, mcp, models, upgrade, ...) plus logging setup, a one-time JSON-to-SQLite migration with a progress bar, and centralized fatal error formatting. The root README.md gives the front-page story — an open source AI coding agent installable via curl/npm/brew/nix with a desktop beta — and the root package.json defines the Bun workspace monorepo (packages/*, packages/sdk/js) that every later step lives in. Keep this map in mind: the tour descends from this entry into the session core, moves out to the clients, and ends at release.
tour.languageLesson: Bun workspaces: the root package.json's `workspaces` globs let packages import each other via `workspace:*`, while `catalog:` offloads dependency versions to a central table in bun.lock — bump once, upgrade everywhere.

tour.title: CLI Run Modes
tour.description: `opencode run` (cli/cmd/run.ts) is the command most users type first, with three modes: non-interactive single-prompt streaming to stdout, interactive local mode booting the split-footer direct UI with an in-process server, and attach mode against an already-running server. It also handles slash-command execution, JSON event output, and session continue/fork. Notice that command handlers flow through cli/effect-cmd.ts (fan-in 25): like everything in this codebase, the CLI is built on Effect services rather than bare promises.
tour.languageLesson: effectCmd adapts yargs handlers to Effect: each handler returns `Effect<void, CliError, ...>`, so CLI subcommands participate in structured concurrency and typed error handling instead of raw async functions.

tour.title: Config & Instance State
tour.description: Every subcommand eventually loads configuration through config/config.ts — the full opencode.json schema (agents, providers, MCP, LSP, compaction, permissions, plugins) deep-merged across global, project, remote well-known, account/org, and MDM sources with variable substitution. Beneath it sits effect/instance-state.ts, the most-imported file in the package (fan-in 63): a per-directory ScopedCache that lazily initializes state for each project instance and invalidates it on dispose, backing instance-scoped services like Env, File, and Format. These two files establish the pattern you will see everywhere: schema-defined state plus Effect layers scoped to a project directory.
tour.languageLesson: Effect's ScopedCache gives InstanceState its power: per-directory lazy initialization with automatic invalidation on dispose — a scoped service registry rather than a global singleton map.

tour.title: Sessions, Events & Persistence
tour.description: The data backbone: session/session.ts is the core Session service (create/fork/get/list plus message and part updates) whose writes flow through SyncEvent projections rather than direct SQL, while bus/index.ts (fan-in 47) is the typed PubSub event bus fanning those events out to every subscriber. storage/db.ts provides a lazy singleton SQLite client — WAL and busy_timeout pragmas, bundled Drizzle migrations — and session/session.sql.ts defines the schema: session, message, part, todo, session_message, and permission tables with cascading foreign keys. message-v2.ts then hydrates those rows back into messages and converts history into AI SDK model messages for the loop you will meet next.
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle convention in this repo: snake_case property names (e.g. `created_at`) so column names never need string overrides, and WAL mode on SQLite so streaming writes do not block concurrent readers.

tour.title: The Agent Loop
tour.description: The heart of the product: session/prompt.ts is the SessionPrompt service wiring twenty-plus Effect services into the agent run loop, and session/loop/run-loop.ts is that loop — each step filters compacted history, dispatches subtask and compaction parts, triggers auto-compaction on overflow, resolves tools, assembles the system prompt suffix, streams the assistant turn, and exits when the assistant finishes without pending tool calls. session/llm.ts wraps the AI SDK's streamText, merging model and agent options and wiring plugin transform hooks around every request. Read run-loop.ts top to bottom: it is the single best file for understanding what an AI coding agent actually does each turn.
tour.languageLesson: The loop is an `Effect.fn` generator running in an Effect fiber: aborting a prompt propagates structured cancellation through the in-flight LLM stream and any nested tool executions — no manual cleanup chains.

tour.title: System Prompt & Agents
tour.description: Who is the agent? system.ts assembles the system prompt: a cacheable prefix joining the shared core.txt with a provider-specific delta chosen by matchDelta's model-ID regex cascade, plus dynamic <environment> and <skills> sections with semantic skill auto-match. agent.ts is the agent registry defining the built-ins (build, plan, general, explore, scout, compaction, title, summary) with layered permission rulesets, merged with user config overrides per instance. These definitions are exactly what Step 5's loop consults on every turn.
tour.languageLesson: Prompt caching economics: the system prompt is split into a stable prefix (core.txt + provider delta) and a dynamic suffix (environment, skills). Keeping the prefix byte-identical across turns lets providers serve it from KV cache instead of re-billing those tokens.

tour.title: Tool Framework
tour.description: Tools are how the loop touches the world. tool/tool.ts defines Tool.define, the framework every tool passes through — schema decoding of arguments, friendly validation errors, automatic output truncation, and OpenTelemetry spans. registry.ts assembles all built-ins plus plugin tools and filters them per model (e.g. apply_patch instead of edit/write for GPT models), while shell.ts and edit.ts show two representative implementations: tree-sitter-parsed command execution, and exact-or-fuzzy file replacement with per-file locking, BOM handling, and LSP diagnostics.
tour.languageLesson: `Tool.define` is a decorator in functional clothing: it takes a tool's execute and returns a wrapped version with decoding, truncation, and telemetry — every built-in tool inherits this behavior without repeating it.

tour.title: Permissions & Subagents
tour.description: Every risky tool call passes through permission/index.ts: ask() evaluates config rules against DB-persisted approvals with deny always winning, waits on a Deferred with a 5-minute timeout, and reply() resolves prompts and transactionally persists 'always allow' rules. tool/task.ts is the subagent spawner — it enforces permission inheritance and nesting limits, applies subagent tool restrictions, and bridges Effect cancellation to abort the child prompt. Together these files form the security boundary between the model's intent and your filesystem.
tour.languageLesson: Permission evaluation flattens all rule sets then uses `findLast` — last match wins. Ordering matters: config deny is checked first, then persisted 'always allow' approvals, then config allow.

tour.title: Provider Layer
tour.description: The provider layer decouples the agent from any single LLM vendor. provider/provider.ts (fan-in 43) merges the models.dev catalog, config, auth, and plugin contributions into the model list and resolves per-provider AI SDK instances with custom fetch and SSE chunk-watchdog wrapping, handling quirks like Azure regions and Bedrock cross-region routing. transform.ts normalizes opencode's internal message contract to each provider via per-provider transform modules, and models.ts caches the models.dev registry with Flock locking and a build-time snapshot fallback. Step 5's llm.ts is the only consumer that needs to care which vendor is behind a model.
tour.languageLesson: The transform layer is the Adapter pattern at message level: one internal message contract, per-provider modules (anthropic, bedrock, mistral, deepseek, ...) that sanitize and reshape it, so the loop never branches on provider IDs.

tour.title: HTTP API Server
tour.description: `opencode serve` exposes the whole agent over HTTP: server/server.ts builds the Effect layer graph, starts the listener with graceful shutdown and optional mDNS discovery, and serves the web handler app plus the public OpenAPI document. The endpoint surface is assembled in httpapi/api.ts (composition root of root, control, global, and instance-scoped route groups) and httpapi/server.ts — the highest fan-out file in the repo at 73 — which wires roughly forty service layers plus auth, CORS, compression, and workspace-routing middleware. This SSE stream plus REST contract is what the TUI, web app, and SDK in the next steps all speak.
tour.languageLesson: Effect HttpApi is schema-first: request and response types are declared as Effect Schemas and compiled into both runtime validators and the OpenAPI document — the same definitions Step 13's SDK generator consumes.

tour.title: Terminal UI Client
tour.description: The flagship client is the OpenTUI terminal app: tui/app.tsx is the root, bootstrapping the renderer, keymap, stderr capture, and the full command palette (session, model, agent, theme, system toggles) with dialogs and the self-upgrade flow. routes/session/index.tsx (fan-out 66) is the complete conversation screen — user and assistant message renderers, per-tool part views, permission and question prompts, and commands like share, rename, fork, compact, and undo/redo. It talks to the Step 10 HTTP API or runs in-process, which is why every interface stays consistent across clients.
tour.languageLesson: OpenTUI renders TSX to the terminal: elements like `<spinner>` and `<markdown>` are custom renderables, and the component tree diffs like a virtual DOM — the session view is effectively a component over the SSE event stream.

tour.title: Web App & Shared UI
tour.description: packages/app is the SolidJS web client: app.tsx composes the full provider stack (query client, i18n, dialogs, SDK, sync, theming, routing), lazy-loads route pages, and gates rendering on a server health check with a connection-error fallback. pages/session.tsx renders the session view — a bounded history window that reveals cached turns on upward scroll, review/diff tabs, a terminal panel, and the composer region. It is built on packages/ui, the shared component library that also serves the desktop app: default-themes.ts ships 38 built-in themes and i18n/en.ts is the English dictionary every other locale falls back to.
tour.languageLesson: SolidJS fine-grained reactivity: use `createResource` (not `createMemo`) when items can be async — this repo documents a regression where swapping in a memo made list dialogs render empty despite 200 OK API calls.

tour.title: Generated TypeScript SDK
tour.description: All clients converge on @opencode-ai/sdk: the root index re-exports the v2 surface and provides createOpencode(), which boots a local server and returns a connected client pair. v2/client.ts wraps the generated hey-api fetch client with a no-timeout fetch, directory and workspace header injection, an HTML-response guard against version-mismatched servers, and structured error wrapping. Crucially, src/v2/gen is generated code — script/build.ts regenerates openapi.json into TypeScript types and the fetch client, then patches the output, so the Step 10 API schema remains the single source of truth.
tour.languageLesson: Never hand-edit generated code: src/v2/gen is rebuilt by script/build.ts from openapi.json via @hey-api/openapi-ts, with a patch step applied after generation. Server schema changes flow one way — regenerate, then adapt consumers.

tour.title: Docs & Release Pipeline
tour.description: The tour ends with how it ships. packages/web is the Astro/Starlight docs and session-share site — content.config.ts registers the docs collections with locale-checked schemas, and rules.mdx is a representative page explaining AGENTS.md rules and precedence. Release runs through .github/workflows/publish.yml (version computation, cross-built binaries, Windows code-signing, npm/GHCR/AUR publishing) gated upstream by ci.yml's typecheck, while packages/opencode/Dockerfile packages the compiled CLI into a minimal multi-stage Alpine image. From entry point to release, you have now traced the full lifecycle of a change in this monorepo.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker with arch selection: both musl binary stages (x64-baseline, arm64) are declared and buildx's TARGETARCH picks one at build time; the runtime stage stays minimal — libgcc, libstdc++, ripgrep — keeping the image small.
